comment: The Quality catalog: for every gtfs-validator notice code, what the validator says about it (from its rules.json) and, where one has been written, the guide the Quality assistant follows. Generated by scripts/build_guides.py from schema/validator/rules.json and schema/guides/*.yaml; do not edit by hand.

mark.label: Pick out these rows among them

speeds.label: Label each leg with its speed

show_value.label: Show a value, invisible characters too

attribution_without_role.description: At least one of the fields `is_producer`, `is_operator`, or `is_authority` should be set to 1.

attributionId.description: The id of the faulty record.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `attributions.txt`, the organisations credited for the feed, credits {{attributionId}} without saying for what. `is_producer`, `is_operator` and `is_authority` are all 0 or empty, so apps cannot show its role.

fix: Set `is_producer`, `is_operator` or `is_authority` to 1 for {{attributionId}}, for each role the organisation played.
If it played none of these roles, remove the row.

bidirectional_exit_gate.summary: Pathway is bidirectional and has mode 7 (exit gate).
bidirectional_exit_gate.description: Exit gates (pathway_mode=7) must not be bidirectional.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the validated record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`, the walkways, gates and elevators inside stations, is an exit gate that is marked as two-way. An exit gate only lets people out, so it has to be one-way.
`pathway_mode` 7 makes it an exit gate, and `is_bidirectional` 1 makes it two-way. Apps may then route riders into the station through a gate that will not open for them.

fix: Set `is_bidirectional` to 0 on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`, with `from_stop_id` the inside of the gate and `to_stop_id` the outside.
If people can also come in through it, give it another `pathway_mode`, such as 6 for a fare gate or 1 for a walkway.

big_gap_in_service.summary: A service has a gap of more than 13 days between active service dates.

gapDurationDays.description: The number of days in the gap.

gapEndDate.description: The last day of the gap.

gapStartDate.description: The first day of the gap.

serviceId.description: The service_id that has the gap.

steps.text: Service {{serviceId}} has {{gapDurationDays|days}} with no trips at all, between {{gapStartDate|date}} and {{gapEndDate|date}}. A break of more than two weeks is often a mistake, such as a missing school term or a mistyped date.
Service days, opened on {{gapStartDate|date}}. Look at the stretch after it where this service has no days.
These are the single days `calendar_dates.txt`, the list of days added to or removed from a service, gives {{serviceId}}. In `exception_type`, 1 adds a day and 2 removes one.

fix: If service {{serviceId}} should run between {{gapStartDate|date}} and {{gapEndDate|date}}, add those days in `calendar.txt` or as added days in `calendar_dates.txt`.
If the break is real, for example a seasonal service, nothing needs to change.

block_trips_with_overlapping_stop_times.summary: Trips with the same block id have overlapping stop times.

csvRowNumberA.description: The row number from `trips.txt` of the first faulty trip.

csvRowNumberB.description: The row number from `trips.txt` of the second faulty trip.

serviceIdA.description: The service id of the first faulty trip.

serviceIdB.description: The service id of the other faulty trip.

tripIdA.description: The id of first faulty trip.

tripIdB.description: The id of the other faulty trip.

steps.text: Trips {{tripIdA}} and {{tripIdB}} share block {{blockId}}, so one vehicle runs them one after the other. On {{intersection|date}} their times overlap: the vehicle would have to be on both at once.
The timetable of {{tripIdA}}, the earlier trip. Note when it reaches its last stop.
{{tripIdB}} leaves before {{tripIdA}} has finished. Apps that tell riders which trip their vehicle continues as cannot trust this block.

fix: If different vehicles run {{tripIdA}} and {{tripIdB}}, give one of them another `block_id`, the column that groups the trips one vehicle runs.
If one vehicle does run both, correct the times in `stop_times.txt` so {{tripIdA}} ends before {{tripIdB}} starts.
If services {{serviceIdA}} and {{serviceIdB}} should not run on the same day, correct their days in `calendar.txt` or `calendar_dates.txt` around {{intersection|date}}.

csv_parsing_failed.summary: Parsing of a CSV file failed.
csv_parsing_failed.description: One common case of the problem is when a cell value contains more than 4096 characters.

charIndex.description: The location of the last character read from before the error occurred.

columnIndex.description: The column index where the exception occurred.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

lineIndex.description: The line number where the exception occurred.

message.description: The detailed message describing the error, and the internal state of the parser/writer.

parsedContent.description: The record number when the exception occurred.

steps.text: The validator could not read `{{filename}}` past line {{lineIndex|from1}}, so the rest of the file was not checked. The usual cause is a value over 4096 characters, or a quote never closed.
Look at column {{columnIndex|from1}} on line {{lineIndex|from1}}: a value far longer than the others, or one that swallows the columns after it.

fix: Open `{{filename}}` in a text editor at line {{lineIndex|from1}} and shorten the value in column {{columnIndex|from1}} to under 4096 characters, or close its quote.
Validate the feed again afterwards, because problems later in `{{filename}}` only show up once it can be read to the end.

decreasing_or_equal_stop_time_distance.description: When sorted by `stop_times.stop_sequence`, two consecutive entries in `stop_times.txt` should have increasing distance, based on the field `shape_dist_traveled`. If the values are equal, this is considered as an error.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `stop_times.txt`.

prevCsvRowNumber.description: The row number from `stop_times.txt` of the previous stop time.

prevShapeDistTraveled.description: Actual distance traveled along the shape from the first shape point to the previous stop time.

shapeDistTraveled.description: Actual distance traveled along the shape from the first shape point to the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty stop.

tripId.description: The id of the faulty trip.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} puts its stop {{stopSequence}} ({{stopId}}) at distance {{shapeDistTraveled|round}} along its line, but its stop {{prevStopSequence}} is already at {{prevShapeDistTraveled|round}}. Each stop has to be further along than the one before.
`shape_dist_traveled`, how far along the line each stop is, should only climb, stop by stop. Apps use it to place the vehicle on the line, and may reject the trip.

fix: Correct `shape_dist_traveled` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt` so stop {{stopId}} is further along than {{prevShapeDistTraveled|round}}.
If the two rows are really the same stop, remove the one listed twice by mistake.
If you cannot measure the distances, leave `shape_dist_traveled` empty for every stop of trip {{tripId}}; apps then place stops by their location.

decreasing_shape_distance.description: When sorted by `shape.shape_pt_sequence`, two consecutive shape points must not have decreasing values for `shape_dist_traveled`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `shapes.txt`.

prevCsvRowNumber.description: The row number from `shapes.txt` of the previous shape point.

prevShapeDistTraveled.description: Actual distance traveled along the shape from the first shape point to the previous shape point.

shapeDistTraveled.description: Actual distance traveled along the shape from the first shape point to the faulty record.

shapeId.description: The id of the faulty shape.

steps.text: Shape {{shapeId}}, a line trips are drawn with, goes backwards: point {{shapePtSequence}} is {{shapeDistTraveled|round}} along it and point {{prevShapePtSequence}}, right next to it, {{prevShapeDistTraveled|round}}. In `shapes.txt`, `shape_dist_traveled` says how far along the line each point is, so it can only grow.

Distance along the line against the order of the points should only climb; the marked points are where it drops. Apps place stops and vehicles on the line by these distances, so a drop can put a vehicle in the wrong place.

fix: Correct `shape_dist_traveled` of point {{shapePtSequence}} or point {{prevShapePtSequence}} of shape {{shapeId}} so the values grow from each point to the next.
If the points themselves are in the wrong order, correct their `shape_pt_sequence` instead.
If the distances cannot be trusted, leave `shape_dist_traveled` empty for the whole shape and for the trips that use it in `stop_times.txt`; apps then work the distances out themselves.

duplicate_fare_media.summary: Two distinct fare media have the same fare media name and type.
duplicate_fare_media.description: Fare media should have a unique combination of fare media name and type.

csvRowNumber1.description: The row number of the first fare media.

csvRowNumber2.description: The row number of the second fare media.

fareMediaId1.description: The id of the first fare media.

fareMediaId2.description: The id of the second fare media.

steps.text: Fare media {{fareMediaId1}} and {{fareMediaId2}} have the same name and type in `fare_media.txt`, the ways riders can pay (a card, a ticket, an app). Riders and apps cannot tell them apart.

fix: If {{fareMediaId1}} and {{fareMediaId2}} are the same card or ticket, delete one and point its fare products in `fare_products.txt` at the other.
If they really are different, give each a `fare_media_name` riders will recognise.

duplicate_geo_json_key.description: The key must be unique for each feature in the GeoJSON file.

firstIndex.description: The index of the first feature with the same key.

secondIndex.description: The index of the other feature with the same key.

steps.text: Zones {{firstIndex|from1}} and {{secondIndex|from1}} of `locations.geojson`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, have the same `id`, {{featureId}}. An id must name one zone, so a trip that points at {{featureId}} could mean either.

fix: If the two zones are the same place, delete one of them from `locations.geojson`.
If they are different places, give one of them a new `id`, and update any `location_id` in `stop_times.txt` that should point at it.

duplicate_geography_id.summary: Geography id is duplicated across multiple files.
duplicate_geography_id.description: ID must be unique across all `stops.stop_id`, `locations.geojson` `id`, and `location_groups.location_group_id` values.

csvRowNumberA.description: The csv row number in stops.txt

csvRowNumberB.description: The csv row number in location_group_stops.txt

geographyId.description: The geography id that is duplicated.

steps.text: The id {{geographyId}} names more than one place. Stops in `stops.txt`, zones in `locations.geojson` and groups of stops in `location_groups.txt` share one set of ids, so a trip that points at {{geographyId}} could mean either.
In `stops.txt`, the list of stops, a row here means {{geographyId}} is also a stop. An empty table means it is not.
In `location_groups.txt`, the groups of stops that on-demand trips serve, a row here means {{geographyId}} is also a group. An empty table means it is not.

fix: Give one of the places a new id, for example {{geographyId}}_zone, and update every row of `stop_times.txt` and `location_group_stops.txt` that points at it.

duplicate_key.description: The values of the given key and rows are duplicates.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file

newCsvRowNumber.description: The row of the other occurrence.

oldCsvRowNumber.description: The row of the first occurrence.

steps.text: Lines {{oldCsvRowNumber}} and {{newCsvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` have the same `{{fieldName1}}`: {{fieldValue1}}. No two rows may share it, so apps keep one and drop the other.

fix: If lines {{oldCsvRowNumber}} and {{newCsvRowNumber}} say the same thing, delete one of them.
If they are meant to be different, change `{{fieldName1}}` on one of them, and anything elsewhere in the feed that uses it.

duplicate_route_name.summary: Two distinct routes have either the same `route_short_name`, the same `route_long_name`, or the same combination of `route_short_name` and `route_long_name`.
duplicate_route_name.description:
All routes of the same `route_type` with the same `agency_id` should have unique combinations of `route_short_name` and `route_long_name`.

Note that there may be valid cases where routes have the same short and long name, e.g., if they serve different areas. However, different directions must be modeled as the same route.

Example of bad data:

route_id | route_short_name | route_long_name
route1 | U1 | Southern
route2 | U1 | Southern

csvRowNumber1.description: The row number of the first occurrence.

csvRowNumber2.description: The row number of the other occurrence.

routeId1.description: The id of the the first occurrence.

routeId2.description: The id of the the other occurrence.

steps.text: Routes {{routeId1}} and {{routeId2}} in `routes.txt`, the list of routes, have the same name, agency and kind of vehicle. In an app's list of routes, riders see two they cannot tell apart.
The trips of {{routeId1}}. `trip_headsign` is the destination shown on the vehicle: note where they go.
The trips of {{routeId2}}. If they run the same line the other way, they belong to route {{routeId1}}: both directions of a route are one route.

fix: If {{routeId2}} is the other direction of {{routeId1}}, give its trips `route_id` {{routeId1}} and `direction_id` 1 in `trips.txt`, and remove route {{routeId2}}.
If they really are different routes, give them names a rider can tell apart, for example a different `route_long_name`.

duplicated_column.description: The input file CSV header has the same column name repeated.

fieldName.description: The name of the faulty field.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: The header of `{{filename}}`, its first line, names `{{fieldName}}` twice: as column {{firstIndex}} and as column {{secondIndex}}. Apps cannot tell which of the two values to use.

fix: Delete one of the two `{{fieldName}}` columns from `{{filename}}`, keeping the one with the right values.
If the second one was meant to be a different column, rename it in the header.

empty_column_name.description: Such columns are skipped by the validator.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

index.description: The index of the empty column.

steps.text: Column {{index}} of `{{filename}}` has no name in the header, the file's first line. The validator skips it, and apps cannot tell what its values mean.

fix: Give column {{index}} of `{{filename}}` its name in the header, or delete the column if it is not needed.
Look for two commas in a row in the header, or a comma at its end: that is the usual cause.

empty_file.description: Empty csv file found in the archive: file does not have any headers, or is a required file and does not have any data. The GTFS specification requires the first line of each file to contain field names and required files must have data.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: `{{filename}}` is empty: it does not even have a header, the first line that names the columns. Apps may treat the file as broken, or reject the feed.

fix: Remove `{{filename}}` from the feed if it has nothing to say.
If it should have data, fill it in: a header line naming its columns, then at least one row.

empty_row.summary: A row in the input file has only spaces.
empty_row.description: Some CSV parsers, such as Univocity, may misinterpret it as a non-empty row that has a single column which is empty, hence we show a warning.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` holds nothing but spaces. Some apps read it as a row with every value empty, and then report that row as broken.

fix: Delete line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` in a text editor.

equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates.summary: Two consecutive points have equal `shape_dist_traveled` and different lat/lon coordinates in `shapes.txt` and the distance between the two points is greater than the 1.11m.
equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates.description: When sorted by `shape.shape_pt_sequence`, the values for `shape_dist_traveled` must increase along a shape. Two consecutive points with equal values for `shape_dist_traveled` and different coordinates indicate an error.

actualDistanceBetweenShapePoints.description: Actual distance traveled along the shape from the first shape point to the previous shape point.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `shapes.txt`.

prevCsvRowNumber.description: The row number from `shapes.txt` of the previous shape point.

shapeId.description: The id of the faulty shape.

steps.text: Points {{prevShapePtSequence}} and {{shapePtSequence}} of shape {{shapeId}}, a line trips are drawn with, are {{actualDistanceBetweenShapePoints|m}} apart, yet both are {{shapeDistTraveled|round}} along it. In `shapes.txt`, `shape_dist_traveled` says how far along the line each point is, so it must grow as the line moves on.
Side by side: different places, the same distance. Apps place stops and vehicles on the line by these distances, so along this stretch they put them in the wrong place.

fix: Raise `shape_dist_traveled` of point {{shapePtSequence}} of shape {{shapeId}} above {{prevShapeDistTraveled|round}} by the {{actualDistanceBetweenShapePoints|m}} between the two points, in the unit the shape uses, and raise every later point by as much.
If the distances cannot be trusted, leave `shape_dist_traveled` empty for the whole shape and for the trips that use it in `stop_times.txt`; apps then work the distances out themselves.

equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates_di.summary: Two consecutive points have equal `shape_dist_traveled` and different lat/lon coordinates in `shapes.txt` and the distance between the two points is greater than 0 but less than 1.11m.
equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates_di.description: When sorted by `shape.shape_pt_sequence`, the values for `shape_dist_traveled` must increase along a shape. Two consecutive points with equal values for `shape_dist_traveled` and small difference of coordinates (greater than 0 but less than 1.11 m distance) result in a warning.

actualDistanceBetweenShapePoints.description: Actual distance traveled along the shape from the first shape point to the previous shape point.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `shapes.txt`.

prevCsvRowNumber.description: The row number from `shapes.txt` of the previous shape point.

shapeId.description: The id of the faulty shape.

steps.text: Points {{prevShapePtSequence}} and {{shapePtSequence}} of shape {{shapeId}}, a line trips are drawn with, are only {{actualDistanceBetweenShapePoints|m}} apart, and both are {{shapeDistTraveled|round}} along it. In `shapes.txt`, `shape_dist_traveled` says how far along the line each point is.
Side by side, they differ only in the last digits of their position. Riders will not notice, but it is usually a point added twice by mistake.

fix: Remove one of the two points, for example line {{csvRowNumber}} of `shapes.txt` (point {{shapePtSequence}} of shape {{shapeId}}).
If both points are needed, make `shape_dist_traveled` of point {{shapePtSequence}} slightly larger than {{prevShapeDistTraveled|round}}.

equal_shape_distance_same_coordinates.summary: Two consecutive points have equal `shape_dist_traveled` and the same lat/lon coordinates in `shapes.txt`.
equal_shape_distance_same_coordinates.description: When sorted by `shape.shape_pt_sequence`, the values for `shape_dist_traveled` must increase along a shape. Two consecutive points with equal values for `shape_dist_traveled` and the same coordinates indicate a duplicative shape point.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `shapes.txt`.

prevCsvRowNumber.description: The row number from `shapes.txt` of the previous shape point.

prevShapeDistTraveled.description: Actual distance traveled along the shape from the first shape point to the previous shape point.

shapeDistTraveled.description: Actual distance traveled along the shape from the first shape point to the faulty record.

shapeId.description: The id of the faulty shape.

steps.text: Points {{prevShapePtSequence}} and {{shapePtSequence}} of shape {{shapeId}}, a line trips are drawn with, are the same point twice: same place, and both {{shapeDistTraveled|round}} along the line. In `shapes.txt`, `shape_dist_traveled` says how far along the line each point is.
Side by side, only the point number differs. The copy changes nothing on the map, but it makes the file longer and can confuse tools that expect each point to move the line on.

fix: Remove line {{csvRowNumber}} of `shapes.txt`, the copy (point {{shapePtSequence}} of shape {{shapeId}}).

expired_calendar.summary: Dataset should not contain date ranges for services that have already expired.
expired_calendar.description: This warning takes into account the `calendar_dates.txt` file as well as the `calendar.txt` file.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

serviceId.description: The service id of the faulty record.

steps.text: Service {{serviceId}} has no days left to run: its last day had already passed when the feed was checked. This is its row on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `calendar.txt`, the weekly pattern of days each service runs.
Service days shows when the feed has service. {{serviceId}} has no days left there. Riders see nothing wrong, but old services make the feed harder to keep up to date.
These are the single days `calendar_dates.txt`, the list of days added or removed, gives {{serviceId}}, if any. They are all in the past too.

fix: If service {{serviceId}} has ended, remove its row from `calendar.txt`, its days in `calendar_dates.txt` and the trips that use it.
If it is still running, set `end_date` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `calendar.txt` to its real last day and mark the weekdays it runs with 1.
A service marked 0 for every weekday only runs on the days `calendar_dates.txt` adds, so it can run out even when its `end_date` is still ahead.

fare_product_with_multiple_default_rider.summary: This notice is generated when a fare product is associated with multiple rider categories that are marked as default.
fare_product_with_multiple_default_rider.description: Each fare product should have at most one default rider category.

csvRowNumber1.description: The CSV row number of the first occurrence of the default rider category

csvRowNumber2.description: The CSV row number of the second occurrence of the default rider category

fareProductId.description: The ID of the fare product associated with the notice

riderCategoryId1.description: The ID of the first rider category that is marked as default

riderCategoryId2.description: The ID of the second rider category that is marked as default

steps.text: Fare product {{fareProductId}} has a price for {{riderCategoryId1}} and one for {{riderCategoryId2}}, and both are marked as the default. `fare_products.txt` lists the fares riders can buy, one row per price.

In `rider_categories.txt`, the kinds of rider (adult, senior, student), both have `is_default_fare_category` set to 1. Apps show the default price to riders who have not said who they are, so a fare can have only one.

fix: Choose which of {{riderCategoryId1}} and {{riderCategoryId2}} is the default, usually the standard adult fare, and set `is_default_fare_category` to 0 for the other in `rider_categories.txt`.

fare_transfer_rule_duration_limit_type_w.summary: A row from GTFS file `fare_transfer_rules.txt` has a defined `duration_limit_type` field but no `duration_limit` specified.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `fare_transfer_rules.txt`, what a transfer between two fares costs, says how the transfer's time limit is counted (`duration_limit_type`) but not how long it is (`duration_limit`). Apps cannot tell riders how long the transfer price lasts.

fix: If the transfer has a time limit, put its length in seconds in `duration_limit` on line {{csvRowNumber}}, for example 5400 for 90 minutes.
If the transfer has no time limit, empty `duration_limit_type` on line {{csvRowNumber}}.

fare_transfer_rule_duration_limit_withou.summary: A row from GTFS file `fare_transfer_rules.txt` has a defined `duration_limit` field but no `duration_limit_type` specified.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `fare_transfer_rules.txt`, what a transfer between two fares costs, gives the transfer a time limit (`duration_limit`, in seconds) but not when that time starts and stops counting (`duration_limit_type`). Apps cannot tell riders if they are still within it.

fix: Set `duration_limit_type` on line {{csvRowNumber}} to say how the time limit is counted.
Use 0 to count from boarding the first vehicle to getting off the next, or 1 from boarding the first to boarding the next.
Use 2 to count from getting off the first vehicle to boarding the next, or 3 from getting off the first to getting off the next.
If the transfer has no time limit, empty `duration_limit` on line {{csvRowNumber}} instead.

fare_transfer_rule_invalid_transfer_coun.summary: A row from GTFS file `fare_transfer_rules.txt` has a defined `transfer_count` with an invalid value.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

transferCount.description: The transfer count value of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `fare_transfer_rules.txt`, what a transfer between two fares costs, allows {{transferCount}} transfers (`transfer_count`). The number must be 1 or more, or -1 for no limit, so apps cannot use this rule.

fix: Set `transfer_count` on line {{csvRowNumber}} to the number of transfers riders may make at this price, or to -1 if there is no limit.
If transfers are not allowed at this price at all, delete line {{csvRowNumber}}.

fare_transfer_rule_missing_transfer_coun.summary: A row from `fare_transfer_rules.txt` has `from_leg_group_id` equal to `to_leg_group_id`, but has no `transfer_count` specified.
fare_transfer_rule_missing_transfer_coun.description: Per the spec, `transfer_count` is required if the two leg group ids are equal.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `fare_transfer_rules.txt`, what a transfer between two fares costs, is a transfer within one group of fares (`from_leg_group_id` and `to_leg_group_id` are the same). It does not say how many such transfers riders may make (`transfer_count`).

fix: Set `transfer_count` on line {{csvRowNumber}} to the number of transfers riders may make at this price, or to -1 if there is no limit.

fare_transfer_rule_with_forbidden_transf.summary: A row from `fare_transfer_rules.txt` has `from_leg_group_id` not equal to `to_leg_group_id`, but has `transfer_count` specified.
fare_transfer_rule_with_forbidden_transf.description: Per the spec, `transfer_count` is forbidden if the two leg group ids are not equal.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `fare_transfer_rules.txt`, what a transfer between two fares costs, is a transfer between two different groups of fares, yet it gives a number of transfers (`transfer_count`). That number is only for transfers within one group.

fix: Empty `transfer_count` on line {{csvRowNumber}}.
To limit transfers within one group, add a row whose `from_leg_group_id` and `to_leg_group_id` are that group, and give the limit there.

fare_transfer_rule_without_transfer_coun.summary: A row from `fare_transfer_rules.txt` has `from_leg_group_id` equal to `to_leg_group_id`, but has no `transfer_count` specified.
fare_transfer_rule_without_transfer_coun.description: Per the spec, `transfer_count` is required if the two leg group ids are equal.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `fare_transfer_rules.txt`, what a transfer between two fares costs, is a transfer within one group of fares (`from_leg_group_id` and `to_leg_group_id` are the same). It does not say how many such transfers riders may make (`transfer_count`).

fix: Set `transfer_count` on line {{csvRowNumber}} to the number of transfers riders may make at this price, or to -1 if there is no limit.

fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops.summary: A transit vehicle moves too fast between two consecutive stops.
fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops.description:
The speed threshold depends on route type:

Route type | Description | Threshold, km/h
0 | Light rail | 100
1 | Subway | 150
2 | Rail | 500
3 | Bus | 150
4 | Ferry | 80
5 | Cable tram | 30
6 | Aerial lift | 50
7 | Funicular | 50
11 | Trolleybus | 150
12 | Monorail | 150
- | Unknown | 200

csvRowNumber1.description: The row number of the first stop time.

csvRowNumber2.description: The row number of the second stop time.

tripCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the problematic trip.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} leaves {{stopName1}} at {{departureTime1}} and reaches the next stop, {{stopName2}}, {{distanceKm|km}} away, at {{arrivalTime2}}: {{speedKph|kmh}}. The marker on the map runs the trip at its scheduled pace.
Each leg labelled with its speed. No vehicle of this kind goes that fast, so riders cannot trust these times and some apps leave the trip out. Usually a time is wrong, or a stop is misplaced.
{{stopName2}} is {{distanceKm|km}} from {{stopName1}} as the crow flies. If either stop is not where it really is, correct its position in `stops.txt`, the list of stops.
Trip {{tripId}} in its route's timetable: compare its times with the trips around it.

fix: Correct the `departure_time` at {{stopName1}} or the `arrival_time` at {{stopName2}} for trip {{tripId}} in `stop_times.txt`, so the trip takes a realistic time to cover {{distanceKm|km}}.
If a stop is in the wrong place, correct its `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` in `stops.txt`.
If the vehicle really is that fast, check `route_type` of route {{routeId}}: the speed allowed depends on the kind of vehicle.

fast_travel_between_far_stops.summary: A transit vehicle moves too fast between two far stops.
fast_travel_between_far_stops.description:
Two stops are considered "far" if they are more than 10 km apart. This normally indicates a more serious problem than too fast travel between consecutive stops.

The speed threshold depends on route type and are the same as `fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops`.

csvRowNumber1.description: The row number of the first stop time.

csvRowNumber2.description: The row number of the second stop time.

tripCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the problematic trip.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} leaves {{stopName1}} at {{departureTime1}} and reaches {{stopName2}}, {{distanceKm|km}} on, at {{arrivalTime2}}: an average of {{speedKph|kmh}}. The marker on the map runs the trip at its scheduled pace.

Each leg labelled with its speed. Over more than 10 km this is no rounded minute: a time is badly wrong, or a stop is far from where it really is. Riders cannot trust these times, and some apps leave the trip out.
{{stopName2}} is {{distanceKm|km}} from {{stopName1}} as the crow flies. If either stop is not where it really is, correct its position in `stops.txt`, the list of stops.
Trip {{tripId}} in its route's timetable: compare its times with the trips around it.

fix: Correct the `departure_time` at {{stopName1}} or the `arrival_time` at {{stopName2}} for trip {{tripId}} in `stop_times.txt`, so the trip takes a realistic time to cover {{distanceKm|km}}.
If a stop is in the wrong place, correct its `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` in `stops.txt`.
If the vehicle really is that fast, check `route_type` of route {{routeId}}: the speed allowed depends on the kind of vehicle.

feed_expiration_date30_days.summary: Dataset should cover at least the next 30 days of service.
feed_expiration_date30_days.description: At any time, the GTFS dataset should cover at least the next 30 days of service, and ideally for as long as the operator is confident that the schedule will continue to be operated.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: `feed_info.txt`, the feed's description of itself, says the feed ends on {{feedEndDate|date}}. It was checked on {{currentDate|date}}, so it covers less than the next 30 days.
A feed should always cover at least the next 30 days, here up to {{suggestedExpirationDate|date}}. After {{feedEndDate|date}}, apps may drop the feed and riders see no trips.

fix: Publish a feed whose schedule runs at least to {{suggestedExpirationDate|date}}, and set `feed_end_date` in `feed_info.txt` to match.
If the schedule after {{feedEndDate|date}} is not final yet, publish the expected one now and update it later.

feed_expiration_date7_days.summary: Dataset should be valid for at least the next 7 days.
feed_expiration_date7_days.description: The dataset expiration date defined in `feed_info.txt` is in seven days or less. At any time, the published GTFS dataset should be valid for at least the next 7 days.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: `feed_info.txt`, the feed's description of itself, says the feed ends on {{feedEndDate|date}}. It was checked on {{currentDate|date}}, so it covers less than the next 7 days.
A feed should always cover at least the next 7 days, here up to {{suggestedExpirationDate|date}}. After {{feedEndDate|date}}, apps may drop the feed and riders see no trips.

fix: Publish a feed whose schedule runs at least to {{suggestedExpirationDate|date}}, and set `feed_end_date` in `feed_info.txt` to match.
If the schedule after {{feedEndDate|date}} is not final yet, publish the expected one now and update it later.

feed_info_lang_and_agency_lang_mismatch.summary: Mismatching feed and agency language fields.
feed_info_lang_and_agency_lang_mismatch.description:
Files `agency.txt` and `feed_info.txt` should define matching `agency.agency_lang` and `feed_info.feed_lang`. The default language may be multilingual for datasets with the original text in multiple languages. In such cases, the `feed_lang` field should contain the language code `mul` defined by the norm ISO 639-2.

- If `feed_lang` is not `mul` and does not match with `agency_lang`, that's an error. - If there is more than one `agency_lang` and `feed_lang` isn't `mul`, that's an error. - If `feed_lang` is `mul` and there isn't more than one `agency_lang`, that's an error.

agencyId.description: The agency id of the faulty record.

agencyLang.description: The agency language of the faulty record.

agencyName.description: The agency name of the faulty record.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

feedLang.description: The feed language of the faulty record.

steps.text: {{agencyName}} gives its language as {{agencyLang}} in `agency.txt`, the list of agencies. The feed as a whole says its texts are in {{feedLang}}.
This is `feed_lang` in `feed_info.txt`, the feed's description of itself. Apps use it to know what language stop names and other texts are in, to show them or read them aloud.

fix: If all texts are in one language, set `agency_lang` for {{agencyName}} and `feed_lang` to the same code.
If the feed's texts really are in several languages, set `feed_lang` to mul.

feed_valid_beyond_total_service_window.summary: The feed is valid 14 days beyond its total service window.

feedEndDate.description: The feed end date from feed_info.txt.

feedStartDate.description: The feed start date from feed_info.txt.

serviceWindowEndDate.description: The latest active service date across all services.

serviceWindowStartDate.description: The earliest active service date across all services.

steps.text: `feed_info.txt`, the feed's description of itself, says the feed is valid from {{feedStartDate|date}} to {{feedEndDate|date}}. Its services only run from {{serviceWindowStartDate|date}} to {{serviceWindowEndDate|date}}.
So for more than two weeks of the period the feed claims, it has no trips at all. An app trusting those dates would show riders an empty timetable.

fix: Set `feed_start_date` and `feed_end_date` in `feed_info.txt` so they stay within the days with service, {{serviceWindowStartDate|date}} to {{serviceWindowEndDate|date}}.
If the feed should have service on the other days, add it in `calendar.txt` or `calendar_dates.txt`.

forbidden_arrival_or_departure_time.summary: The arrival or departure times are provided alongside pickup or drop-off windows in `stop_times.txt`.
forbidden_arrival_or_departure_time.description: This violates GTFS specification, as both cannot coexist for a single stop time record.

arrivalTime.description: The arrival time of the faulty record.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

departureTime.description: The departure time of the faulty record.

endPickupDropOffWindow.description: The end pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

startPickupDropOffWindow.description: The start pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, gives both a fixed time and a pickup and drop-off window, {{startPickupDropOffWindow}} to {{endPickupDropOffWindow}}. A window is for flex service: a zone or a time window, booked in advance, rather than fixed stops at fixed times.
A row is either a stop at a set time or a window, never both. With both, apps cannot tell riders when the vehicle comes.

fix: If the service runs on demand, empty `arrival_time` and `departure_time` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt` and keep the window.
If the vehicle comes at a set time, keep the times and empty `start_pickup_drop_off_window` and `end_pickup_drop_off_window`.

forbidden_continuous_pickup_drop_off.summary: Continuous pickup or drop-off are forbidden when routes.continuous_pickup or routes.continuous_drop_off are 0, 2 or 3 and stop_times.start_pickup_drop_off_window or stop_times.end_pickup_drop_off_window are defined for any trip of this route.

endPickupDropOffWindow.description: The end time of the pickup/drop-off window.

routeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the route in the `routes.txt` file.

startPickupDropOffWindow.description: The start time of the pickup/drop-off window.

stopTimeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the stop time in the `stop_times.txt` file.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} is a flex trip: it serves a zone or a time window, booked in advance, rather than fixed stops at fixed times. Line {{stopTimeCsvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, gives it the window {{startPickupDropOffWindow}} to {{endPickupDropOffWindow}}.

But its route, on line {{routeCsvRowNumber}} of `routes.txt`, lets riders get on or off anywhere along the line (`continuous_pickup` or `continuous_drop_off` is 0, 2 or 3). A trip booked by zone has no line to stop along, so apps get conflicting instructions.

fix: On line {{routeCsvRowNumber}} of `routes.txt`, set `continuous_pickup` and `continuous_drop_off` to 1, meaning no stopping along the line, or leave them empty.
If other trips of the route do stop anywhere along the line, move flex trips such as {{tripId}} to a route of their own.

forbidden_drop_off_type.summary: pickup_drop_off_window fields are forbidden when the drop_off_type is regularly scheduled (0).

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

endPickupDropOffWindow.description: The end pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

startPickupDropOffWindow.description: The start pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, gives a pickup and drop-off window, {{startPickupDropOffWindow}} to {{endPickupDropOffWindow}}. But its `drop_off_type`, how riders get off, is 0: a regular drop-off at a scheduled time.
A window is for flex service: a zone or a time window, booked in advance, rather than fixed stops at fixed times. It has no scheduled time to get off at, so the two contradict each other.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, set `drop_off_type` to 1 if riders cannot get off here, 2 if they must phone to arrange it, or 3 if they arrange it with the driver.
If this really is a regular scheduled stop, remove the window and give the row an arrival and departure time instead.

forbidden_geography_id.summary: A stop_time entry has more than one geographical id defined.
forbidden_geography_id.description: In stop_times.txt, you can have only one of stop_id, location_group_id or location_id defined for given entry.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id that already exists.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, names both stop {{stopId}} and zone {{locationId}}. A row must name exactly one of a stop (`stop_id`), a zone (`location_id`) or a group of stops (`location_group_id`), or apps cannot tell where the vehicle goes.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, keep only the place this row is about: `stop_id` {{stopId}} for a fixed stop, or `location_id` {{locationId}} for a zone served on demand.
If the trip really serves both, split this into two rows, each with its own `stop_sequence`.

forbidden_pickup_type.summary: pickup_drop_off_window fields are forbidden when the pickup_type is regularly scheduled (0) or must be coordinated with the driver (3).

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

endPickupDropOffWindow.description: The end pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

startPickupDropOffWindow.description: The start pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, gives a pickup and drop-off window, {{startPickupDropOffWindow}} to {{endPickupDropOffWindow}}. But its `pickup_type`, how riders get on, is 0 (a scheduled pickup) or 3 (arranged with the driver at the stop).
A window is for flex service: a zone or a time window, booked in advance, rather than fixed stops at fixed times. Neither a scheduled pickup nor one arranged at the stop fits that.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, set `pickup_type` to 2 if riders must phone to book, or 1 if they cannot get on here.
If this really is a regular scheduled stop, remove the window and give the row an arrival and departure time instead.

forbidden_prior_day_booking_field_value.summary: A forbidden field value is present for a prior-day booking rule in `booking_rules.txt`

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

fieldNames.description: The names of the forbidden fields comma-separated.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) is for trips booked one or more days before (`booking_type` 2). Yet it also fills in `{{fieldNames}}`, used only for trips booked the same day.
A deadline days ahead is a day and a time (`prior_notice_last_day`, `prior_notice_last_time`). With a number of minutes as well, an app cannot tell riders which deadline is true.

fix: Empty `{{fieldNames}}` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}}, and keep the deadline in `prior_notice_last_day` and `prior_notice_last_time`.
If riders actually book the same day, set `booking_type` to 1 and empty the `prior_notice_last_` and `prior_notice_start_` columns instead.

forbidden_prior_notice_start_day.summary: `prior_notice_start_day` value is forbidden when `prior_notice_duration_max` is set.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) says riders can book at most {{priorNoticeDurationMax}} minutes before the trip (`prior_notice_duration_max`), and also from {{priorNoticeStartDay|days}} before (`prior_notice_start_day`). Only one of the two may say when booking opens.

fix: If booking opens a number of minutes before the trip, empty `prior_notice_start_day` and `prior_notice_start_time` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}}.
If booking opens on a day before the trip, empty `prior_notice_duration_max` and set `booking_type` to 2, booking one or more days before.

forbidden_prior_notice_start_time.summary: `prior_notice_start_time` value is forbidden when `prior_notice_start_day` value is not set in booking_rules.txt.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) says booking opens at {{priorNoticeStartTime}} (`prior_notice_start_time`), but not how many days before the trip (`prior_notice_start_day`). Without a day, apps cannot tell riders when booking opens.

fix: Set `prior_notice_start_day` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} to the number of days before the trip that booking opens at {{priorNoticeStartTime}}.
If there is no earliest time to book, empty `prior_notice_start_time` instead.

forbidden_real_time_booking_field_value.summary: A forbidden field value is present for a real-time booking rule in `booking_rules.txt`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

fieldNames.description: The names of the forbidden fields comma-separated.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) is for trips booked in real time, up to the moment of travel (`booking_type` 0). Yet it also fills in `{{fieldNames}}`, used only when riders must book ahead.
Booking in real time has no deadline. With one filled in as well, an app cannot tell riders whether they have to book ahead.

fix: Empty `{{fieldNames}}` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}}.
If riders do have to book ahead, set `booking_type` to 1 (the same day) or 2 (one or more days before) and keep the deadline.

forbidden_same_day_booking_field_value.summary: A forbidden field value is present for a same-day booking rule in `booking_rules.txt`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

fieldNames.description: The names of the forbidden fields comma-separated.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) is for trips booked earlier the same day (`booking_type` 1). Yet it also fills in `{{fieldNames}}`, used only for trips booked days before.
A same-day deadline is a number of minutes before the trip (`prior_notice_duration_min`). With a deadline in days as well, an app cannot tell riders which one is true.

fix: Empty `{{fieldNames}}` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}}, and give the notice riders must give, in minutes, in `prior_notice_duration_min`.
If riders actually book one or more days before, set `booking_type` to 2 and empty `prior_notice_duration_min` and `prior_notice_duration_max` instead.

forbidden_shape_dist_traveled.summary: A stop_time entry has a `shape_dist_traveled` without a `stop_id` value.
forbidden_shape_dist_traveled.description: A GeoJSON location or location group has an associated shape_dist_traveled field in stop_times.txt. shape_dist_traveled values should only be provided for stops.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

locationGroupId.description: The location_grpup_id for which the shape_dist_traveled is defined

locationId.description: The location_id for which the shape_dist_traveled is defined

tripId.description: The trip_id for which the shape_dist_traveled is defined

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, gives trip {{tripId}} a `shape_dist_traveled` of {{shapeDistTraveled|round}}, a distance along its line, at a zone rather than a stop. A vehicle can be anywhere in a zone, so no single distance fits, and apps may time the trip wrongly.

fix: Empty `shape_dist_traveled` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, since it is only for rows that name a stop in `stop_id`.

foreign_key_violation.description: A foreign key references the primary key of another file. A foreign key violation means that the foreign key referenced from a given row (the child file) cannot be found in the corresponding file (the parent file). The Foreign keys are defined in the specification under "Type" for each file.

childFieldName.description: The name of the field that makes reference.

childFilename.description: The name of the file from which reference is made.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

parentFieldName.description: The name of the field that is referred to.

parentFilename.description: The name of the file that is referred to.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{childFilename}}` points to `{{childFieldName}}` {{fieldValue}}, which is not in `{{parentFilename}}`. Apps cannot follow the link, so they may drop this row, or its whole trip.
Searching `{{parentFilename}}` for `{{parentFieldName}}` {{fieldValue}} finds nothing.

fix: Add a row with `{{parentFieldName}}` {{fieldValue}} to `{{parentFilename}}`.
If line {{csvRowNumber}} is the one that is wrong, change its `{{childFieldName}}` to one that exists; a typo or a space at the end is the usual cause.

future_calendar.summary: All services in the feed start in the future; no service covers today's date.

minServiceStartDate.description: The earliest service start date across all services in the feed.

steps.text: The feed was checked on {{currentDate|date}}, but its first day of service is {{minServiceStartDate|date}}. Until then, an app using only this feed has no trips to show riders.
Service days, opened on {{minServiceStartDate|date}}, the first day with trips.

fix: If this feed is published ahead of a new schedule, keep the current feed available until {{minServiceStartDate|date}}, or merge the two into one feed.
If the services should already be running, correct `start_date` in `calendar.txt` or the days in `calendar_dates.txt`.

future_feed.summary: The feed covers the future only.
future_feed.description: The minimum `start_date` in `feed_info.txt` is greater than today's date, indicating the feed covers the future only.

steps.text: `feed_info.txt`, the feed's description of itself, says the feed starts on {{feedStartDate|date}}. It was checked on {{currentDate|date}}, so it covers only the future.

fix: If this feed is published ahead of a new schedule, keep the current feed available until {{feedStartDate|date}}.
If the feed should already be in use, correct `feed_start_date` in `feed_info.txt`.

duplicatedElement.description: The duplicated element in the GeoJSON file.

filename.description: The name of the file where the duplicated element was found.

steps.text: `{{filename}}`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, gives `{{duplicatedElement}}` twice in the same place. Apps keep only one of the two, and which one is not defined, so riders may see the wrong zones or none.

fix: Open `{{filename}}` in a text editor, find the two `{{duplicatedElement}}` entries, and delete the one that is wrong.

filename.description: The name of the file where the unknown element was found.

unknownElement.description: The unknown element in the GeoJSON file.

steps.text: `{{filename}}`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, contains `{{unknownElement}}`, which GTFS does not define for that file. Apps ignore it. That is harmless for a note to yourself, but if it was meant to describe a zone, riders never see it.

actions.label: The name GTFS does not know

fix: If `{{unknownElement}}` is misspelt or sits at the wrong level of `{{filename}}`, rename or move it to what GTFS expects.
If it is extra information for your own tools, you can leave it as it is.

message.description: The error message that explains the reason for the exception.

steps.text: This is not a problem in the feed's data: the validator could not read or write a file it needed. The rest of the report may be incomplete.

fix: Run the validator again, after checking that the feed file opens and that there is enough disk space.
If it happens again, report it to the gtfs-validator project on GitHub, with the message above and the error name {{exception}}.

inconsistent_agency_lang.description: Agencies from GTFS `agency.txt` have been found to have different languages.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `agency.txt`, the list of agencies, gives its language as {{actual}}, while the other agencies use {{expected}}. Apps expect one language for the feed, so some texts may be shown or read aloud wrongly.

fix: If the agency's texts are in {{expected}}, set `agency_lang` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `agency.txt` to {{expected}}.
If the feed really mixes languages, set `feed_lang` in `feed_info.txt` to mul and add translations in `translations.txt`.

inconsistent_agency_timezone.description: Agencies from GTFS `agency.txt` have been found to have different timezones.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `agency.txt`, the list of agencies, gives its time zone as {{actual}}, while the other agencies use {{expected}}. All agencies in one feed must share a time zone, because every time in the timetable is read in it.
With two time zones, apps cannot tell which one the departure times mean. They may show times shifted, or reject the feed.

fix: If that agency's times are in {{expected}}, set `agency_timezone` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `agency.txt` to {{expected}}.
If the agency really runs in {{actual}}, publish it in a separate feed, with its times written in its own zone.

inconsistent_route_type_for_block_id.summary: A block should have the same route mode.

blockId.description: The block_id value of the faulty trip.

routeIds.description: The route_id values associated with the block_id comma separated.

routeTypes.description: The route_type values associated with the block_id comma separated.

steps.text: Block {{blockId}} puts trips of routes {{routeIds}} on one vehicle, but those routes use different kinds of vehicle: {{routeTypes|words}}. One vehicle cannot be both.
In `routes.txt`, the list of routes, `route_type` says what kind of vehicle each route uses. An app telling riders their bus continues as the next trip would announce the wrong vehicle.

fix: If different vehicles run these trips, give them different `block_id` values in `trips.txt`.
If one of routes {{routeIds}} has the wrong `route_type`, correct it in `routes.txt`.

inconsistent_route_type_for_in_seat_tran.summary: An in-seat transfer should occur in the same route mode.

csvRowNumber.description: The csv row number of the faulty transfer in tranfers.txt.

fromRouteId.description: The from_route_id value of the faulty transfer.

fromRouteType.description: The route_type value of the from_route_id.

toRouteId.description: The to_route_id value of the faulty transfer.

toRouteType.description: The route_type value of the to_route_id.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, the connections between services, says riders stay in their seat from {{fromRouteType|words}} route {{fromRouteId}} to {{toRouteType|words}} route {{toRouteId}}.

`route_type` says what kind of vehicle runs a route. Staying seated only works when the same vehicle carries on, and one vehicle cannot run as both {{fromRouteType|words}} and {{toRouteType|words}}. Apps may tell riders to stay on board when they have to change.

fix: If riders really change vehicles, set `transfer_type` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt` to 0, 1 or 2 instead of 4.
If the same vehicle does carry on, correct the `route_type` of {{fromRouteId}} or {{toRouteId}} so both name the same kind of vehicle.

invalid_character.summary: This field contains invalid characters, such as the replacement character ("�").
invalid_character.description: Check that text was properly encoded in UTF-8 as required by GTFS.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number in the CSV file where the invalid characters were found.

fieldName.description: The name of the field containing the invalid characters.

fieldValue.description: The value of the field containing the invalid characters.

filename.description: The name of the file containing the invalid characters.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` has a broken character in `{{fieldName}}`: "{{fieldValue}}". The � sign stands in for a letter that was lost when the file was saved in the wrong text encoding.

Apps show the � to riders exactly as it is, on screens and in spoken announcements, and the missing letter cannot be guessed back. GTFS requires text saved as UTF-8 so that letters such as é, ñ or ü survive.

fix: Type the missing letter back in place of the � in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}`, taking the right spelling from the system the feed is exported from.
Save `{{filename}}` as UTF-8, and check the export does not convert text to another encoding on the way, or the letter will be lost again.

invalid_color.summary: A field contains an invalid color value.
invalid_color.description:
A color must be encoded as a six-digit hexadecimal number. The leading "#" is not included.

Example: `FFFFFF` for white, `000000` for black or `0039A6` for the A,C,E lines in NYC MTA.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not a colour an app can read. Apps cannot draw the route in its colour, and may fall back to a default one or reject the value.
A colour is written as six hexadecimal digits (0 to 9 and A to F) with no # in front: 0000FF is blue, FFFFFF is white, 000000 is black.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with a six-digit colour code, such as 0000FF for blue.
Take the code from the agency's brand colours or its printed maps, so apps draw the route the way riders know it.
If the value has a # in front, remove it.

invalid_currency.summary: A field contains a wrong currency code.
invalid_currency.description:
Currency code must follow ISO 4217

Example: `CAD` for Canadian dollars, `EUR` for euros or `JPY` for Japanese yen.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}`, the currency of the price, the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not a currency code. Apps cannot tell riders what the fare costs without knowing its currency.
A currency is written as its three-letter international code (ISO 4217): CAD for Canadian dollars, USD for US dollars, EUR for euros, JPY for Japanese yen.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the three-letter code of the fare's currency, such as CAD, USD or EUR.

invalid_currency_amount.summary: A currency amount field has a value that does not match the format of its corresponding currency code field.
invalid_currency_amount.description: Typically, this means the amount did not have the expected number of decimal places. Check the formatting of your amount field so it matches the number of decimal places specified by the currency_code value.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value {{fieldValue}} {{currencyCode}}, which does not have the number of decimal places {{currencyCode}} uses. Apps may show the wrong price, or refuse it.
An amount has exactly as many decimals as its currency's smallest coin: two for currencies counted in cents, such as CAD, USD or EUR (3.75), and none for currencies such as JPY (300).

fix: Write `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the decimals {{currencyCode}} uses, rounding {{fieldValue}} to the price riders actually pay, for example 3.75.
If the amount is right but the currency is wrong, correct the currency instead.

invalid_date.summary: A field cannot be parsed as date.
invalid_date.description:
Dates must have the YYYYMMDD format.

Example: `20180913` for September 13th, 2018.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not a real date. Apps cannot tell which days the service runs, and may drop it or reject the feed.
A date is written as year, month and day with nothing between them: 20261015 is 15 October 2026. The month goes from 01 to 12 and the day must exist in that month.

fix: Correct `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` to a real date written as YYYYMMDD, such as 20261231.
If the dates come from a spreadsheet, format the column as plain text so it does not turn them into another date format.

invalid_email.summary: A field contains a malformed email address.
invalid_email.description: Definitions for valid emails are quite vague. We perform strict validation using the Apache Commons EmailValidator.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not an email address. Riders who tap it in an app to get in touch reach no one.
An email address is one name, an @ and a domain, with no spaces and nothing else around it.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with a working address, such as info@example.org.
If there is no address to give, leave `{{fieldName}}` empty, if the column allows it.

invalid_float.summary: A field cannot be parsed as a floating point number.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", where a number is expected. Apps cannot use the row as it is, and may skip it or reject the feed.
A number is written with digits only, a dot for decimals and a minus sign in front if it is negative: no words, units, spaces or commas.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the number it stands for, such as 45.5017.
If the value was typed with a comma for decimals (45,5017), use a dot instead.

invalid_geometry.summary: A polygon in `locations.geojson` is unparsable or invalid.
invalid_geometry.description: Each polygon must be valid by the definition of the OpenGIS Simple Features Specification, section 6.1.11 .

featureId.description: The id of the faulty record.

featureIndex.description: The index of the feature in the feature collection.

geometryType.description: The geometry type of the feature containing the invalid polygon.

steps.text: The outline of zone {{featureId}} in `locations.geojson`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, is not a valid shape. Apps cannot reliably tell whether a rider's address is inside it.
An outline must be a closed line that never crosses itself. Corners listed in the wrong order make it cross over, like a bow tie.

fix: Redraw zone {{featureId}} in a map editor such as QGIS or geojson.io so its outline does not cross itself, and export `locations.geojson` again.
If the zone is really two areas, draw it as a MultiPolygon of two separate outlines.

invalid_input_files_in_subfolder.summary: At least 1 GTFS file is in a subfolder.
invalid_input_files_in_subfolder.description:
All GTFS files must reside at the root level directly. There are two common cases that trigger this error:

1. The root folder (e.g., a folder called "GTFS 2020") was zipped instead of the individual files within the folder (e.g., `calendar.txt`, `agency.txt`, etc.). This can be fixed by zipping the files directly instead. 2. A file associated with GTFS is in a subfolder rather than the root folder of the dataset, and needs to be removed if not needed or moved to the root level.

steps.text: The feed's files are in a folder inside the zip, not at its top level. Apps look only at the top level, so to them the feed has no files.

fix: Select the .txt files themselves and zip them, rather than zipping the folder that holds them.
If a GTFS file is in a subfolder by mistake, move it to the top level, or remove it if it is not needed.

invalid_integer.summary: A field cannot be parsed as an integer.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", where a whole number is expected. Apps cannot use the value, and may skip the row or reject the feed.
A whole number is written with digits only: no words, decimals or spaces. Many columns use numbers as codes, such as 1 for yes and 0 for no.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the number it stands for, for example 1 for yes and 0 for no.

invalid_language_code.summary: A field contains a wrong language code.
invalid_language_code.description:
Language codes must follow IETF BCP 47.

Example: `en` for English, `en-US` for American English or `de` for German.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not a language code. Apps use it to pick the language and the voice they read names in.
A language is written as its short international code: en for English, fr for French, es for Spanish, with a region after a hyphen if needed, such as en-US or fr-CA.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the code of the language the feed's text is written in, such as en or fr.

invalid_phone_number.summary: A field contains a malformed phone number.
invalid_phone_number.description: This rule uses the [PhoneNumberUtil](https://www.javadoc.io/doc/com.googlecode.libphonenumber/libphonenumber/8.4.1/com/google/i18n/phonenumbers/PhoneNumberUtil.html) class to validate a phone number based on a country code. If no country code is provided in the parameters used to run the validator, this notice won't be emitted.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not a phone number that can be dialled in the feed's country. Riders who tap it in an app to call reach no one.
The number is checked against the country given when the validator was run, so it needs all its digits, as a rider would dial them. Spaces, dashes and brackets are fine.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the full number riders should call, such as +1 514-555-0100.
If there is no number to give, leave `{{fieldName}}` empty, if the column allows it.

invalid_pickup_drop_off_window.summary: The pickup/drop-off window in `stop_times.txt` is invalid.
invalid_pickup_drop_off_window.description: The `end_pickup_drop_off_window` must be strictly later than the `start_pickup_drop_off_window`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

endPickupDropOffWindow.description: The end pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

startPickupDropOffWindow.description: The start pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, gives a pickup and drop-off window that starts at {{startPickupDropOffWindow}} and ends at {{endPickupDropOffWindow}}. The end must be later than the start, so there is no time at which riders can be served.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, correct the window so it ends after it starts; if the times are swapped, set `start_pickup_drop_off_window` to {{endPickupDropOffWindow}} and `end_pickup_drop_off_window` to {{startPickupDropOffWindow}}.
A window that runs past midnight is written with hours past 24, for example 22:00:00 to 25:00:00.

invalid_prior_notice_duration_min.summary: An invalid `prior_notice_duration_min` value is present in a booking rule.
invalid_prior_notice_duration_min.description: The `prior_notice_duration_max` field value needs to be greater or equal to the `prior_notice_duration_min` field value.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) asks riders to book at least {{priorNoticeDurationMin}} minutes before the trip, but no more than {{priorNoticeDurationMax}} minutes before. No booking can do both, so booking is never open.

fix: If the two were entered the wrong way round, set `prior_notice_duration_min` to {{priorNoticeDurationMax}} and `prior_notice_duration_max` to {{priorNoticeDurationMin}} for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}}.
Otherwise, make `prior_notice_duration_max` at least {{priorNoticeDurationMin}}, or empty it if there is no earliest time to book.

invalid_row_length.description: A row in the input file has a different number of values than specified by the CSV header.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

headerCount.description: The number of column in the faulty file.

rowLength.description: The length of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` has {{rowLength}} values, but the header names {{headerCount}} columns. There is no telling which value belongs in which column, so apps may skip the row.
Line {{csvRowNumber}} cannot be read safely, so it is left out of the table. The rows around it each have a value, even an empty one, for every column.

fix: Open `{{filename}}` in a text editor at line {{csvRowNumber}} and give it {{headerCount}} values, adding empty ones (two commas in a row) where a value is missing.
If a value contains a comma, put that value in double quotes so it is read as one.

invalid_time.summary: A field cannot be parsed as time.
invalid_time.description:
Time must be in the `H:MM:SS`, `HH:MM:SS` or `HHH:MM:SS` format.

Example: `14:30:00` for 2:30PM or `25:35:00` for 1:35AM on the next day.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not a time. Apps cannot tell riders when the vehicle comes, and may drop the trip or reject the feed.
A time is written as hours, minutes and seconds with colons, on a 24-hour clock: 14:30:00 is 2:30 pm. Past midnight the hours keep counting, so 25:35:00 is 1:35 am the next morning.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the time written as HH:MM:SS, such as 06:00:00.

invalid_timezone.summary: A field cannot be parsed as a timezone.
invalid_timezone.description:
Timezones are defined at www.iana.org. Timezone names never contain the space character but may contain an underscore. Refer to Wikipedia for a list of valid values.

Example: `Asia/Tokyo`, `America/Los_Angeles` or `Africa/Cairo`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not a time zone. Every time in the feed is read in this zone, so apps cannot tell riders when anything runs.
A time zone is written as its name in the international list (IANA): a region and a city, joined by a slash, with underscores for spaces, such as America/Toronto, Europe/Paris or America/Los_Angeles.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the time zone the service runs in, such as America/Toronto.
Use the zone of the city that sets the agency's clock, not an abbreviation such as EST or a number such as -05:00.

invalid_url.summary: A field contains a malformed URL.
invalid_url.description: Definitions for valid URLs are quite vague. We perform strict validation using the Apache Commons UrlValidator.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", which is not a full web address. Riders who tap the link in an app land nowhere.
A web address starts with https:// (or http://), then the site's name, then the page, with no spaces: the way it appears in a browser's address bar.

fix: Replace "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the full address, starting with https://, and check it opens in a browser.

leading_or_trailing_whitespaces.summary: The value in CSV file has leading or trailing whitespaces.
leading_or_trailing_whitespaces.description:
This notice is emitted for values protected with double quotes since whitespaces for non-protected values are trimmed automatically by CSV parser.

The validator strips whitespaces from protected values. We do not see any use case when such a whitespace may be needed. On the other hand, some real-world feeds use trailing whitespaces for some values and omit them for the others. This is causing the largest problem when a primary key and a foreign key differ just by a whitespace: it is clear that they are intended to be the same, that is why we always strip whitespaces.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` has a space at the start or the end of `{{fieldName}}`: "{{fieldValue}}". The marks below show where.
The validator removes such spaces before it checks anything, but other apps may not: text can show out of line, and an id with a space no longer matches the same id written without one.

fix: Remove the space at the start or end of `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}`.
Check the export trims values, since one space usually means others: a tool that adds quotes around values often keeps spaces inside them.

location_with_unexpected_stop_time.summary: A location in `stops.txt` that is not a stop is referenced by some `stop_times.stop_id`.
location_with_unexpected_stop_time.description: Referenced locations (using `stop_times.stop_id`) must be stops/platforms, i.e. their `stops.location_type` value must be 0 or empty.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `stops.txt`.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty record from `stops.txt`.

stopTimeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `stop_times.txt`.

steps.text: Line {{stopTimeCsvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, has a vehicle stop at {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}). But {{stopName}} is not a place where vehicles stop, so apps cannot show riders where to board.
In `stops.txt`, the list of stops, its `location_type` marks it as a whole station, an entrance or another part of a station. Only 0 or empty means a stop or platform where riders get on and off.

fix: On line {{stopTimeCsvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, replace {{stopId}} with the platform inside {{stopName}} where the vehicle stops, a row of `stops.txt` whose `parent_station` is {{stopId}}.
If {{stopName}} really is a stop, set its `location_type` to 0 in `stops.txt`.

location_without_parent_station.summary: A location that must have `parent_station` field does not have it.
location_without_parent_station.description: The following location types must have `parent_station`: entrance, generic node, boarding_area.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty record.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}), line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt`, the list of stops and stations, is part of a station. But its `parent_station` is empty, so nothing says which station.

`location_type` is the kind of place: 0 a stop or platform, 1 a station, 2 an entrance, 3 a node inside a station, 4 a boarding area. This row is a {{locationType}}, which only exists inside a station or platform.

fix: Set `parent_station` of {{stopId}} to the `stop_id` of its station, or, for a boarding area, of its platform.
If {{stopId}} is really a stop on its own, set its `location_type` to 0.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

message.description: The detailed message describing the error.

steps.text: `{{filename}}` could not be read because it is not valid JSON, the text format the file must be written in. When this is `locations.geojson`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, none of its zones can be used. The message says where reading stopped.

fix: Open `{{filename}}` in a text editor or a JSON checker, go to the line and column in the message, and repair the text there.
The usual causes are a file cut short, a missing comma, bracket or quote, or a comma after the last item of a list.
If the file was cut short, export it again from the tool that made it.

missing_bike_allowance.summary: Ferry trips should include bike allowance information.
missing_bike_allowance.description: All ferry trips should have a valid value in the bikes_allowed field in trips.txt.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Ferry trip {{tripId}} does not say whether riders may bring a bike on board. `bikes_allowed`, the column of `trips.txt` that says so, is empty or 0, which means no information.
Its route, {{routeId}}, is a ferry (`route_type` 4). Many ferry riders travel with a bike, and trip planners use this value to plan a journey with one.

fix: Set `bikes_allowed` of trip {{tripId}} to 1 if bikes may come on board, or 2 if they may not.
Do the same for the other trips of route {{routeId}}.

missing_calendar_and_calendar_date_files.description: At least one of the files must be provided.

steps.text: The feed has neither `calendar.txt`, the weekly pattern of days each service runs, nor `calendar_dates.txt`, the list of single days. No trip has a day to run on, so apps show no service and may reject the feed.

fix: Add `calendar.txt`, `calendar_dates.txt` or both, with a row for every `service_id` that the trips in `trips.txt` use.
If the files exist but sit in a folder inside the zip, move all the files to the top level of the zip.

missing_feed_contact_email_and_url.summary: Best Practices for `feed_info.txt` suggest providing at least one of `feed_contact_email` and `feed_contact_url`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the validated record.
