steps.text: `feed_info.txt`, the feed's description of itself, gives no way to contact its publisher: neither `feed_contact_email` nor `feed_contact_url` has a value. Apps and riders who find a mistake have nowhere to report it.

fix: Add `feed_contact_email`, `feed_contact_url` or both to line {{csvRowNumber}} of `feed_info.txt`, for example the address of the team that maintains the feed.

missing_feed_info_date.summary: One of `feed_start_date` or `feed_end_date` is specified, but not both.
missing_feed_info_date.description: Even though `feed_info.start_date` and `feed_info.end_date` are optional, if one field is provided the second one should also be provided.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `feed_info.txt`, the feed's description of itself, gives only one end of the period the feed is valid for: `{{fieldName}}` is empty. Apps cannot tell when the feed stops or starts being valid.

fix: Fill in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `feed_info.txt`, or leave both `feed_start_date` and `feed_end_date` empty.

missing_level_id.description: GTFS file `levels.txt` is required for elevator (`pathway_mode=5`). A row from `stops.txt` linked to an elevator pathway has no value for `stops.level_id`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty stop from `stops.txt`.

stopName.description: The name of the faulty stop from `stops.txt`.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) is at one end of an elevator, but its `level_id`, the floor it is on, is empty.
These are the elevators in `pathways.txt`, the walkways and lifts inside stations. An elevator links two floors, so apps need the floor at each end to tell riders where it goes.
`levels.txt` lists the floors of the stations. The `level_id` of {{stopId}} has to be one of them.

fix: Set `level_id` of {{stopId}} in `stops.txt` to the floor it is on, one of the values in `levels.txt`.
If `levels.txt` does not list that floor yet, add a row for it, with a `level_index` of 0 for street level and negative numbers below.

missing_pickup_drop_off_booking_rule_id.summary: pickup_booking_rule_id is recommended when pickup_type=2 and drop_off_booking_rule_id is recommended when drop_off_type=2.
missing_pickup_drop_off_booking_rule_id.description: Currently, this notice is only triggered on feeds when either start_pickup_drop_off_window or end_pickup_drop_off_window is defined, since this recommendation was added to the specification for feeds with GTFS-Flex.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record in `stop_times.txt`

dropOffType.description: The drop-off type of the faulty record.

pickupType.description: The pickup type of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, says pickup: {{pickupType|words}}, drop-off: {{dropOffType|words}}. Where riders must phone ahead, the row should also say which booking rule applies, and it does not, so riders are not told how or when to book.
The rules are in `booking_rules.txt`: how far ahead to book, until when, and by phone or online.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, set `pickup_booking_rule_id` (for a phoned pickup) or `drop_off_booking_rule_id` (for a phoned drop-off) to the `booking_rule_id` of the rule riders must follow.
If no rule in `booking_rules.txt` describes it yet, add one there first.

missing_pickup_or_drop_off_window.summary: Either the start or end pickup/drop-off window is missing in `stop_times.txt`.
missing_pickup_or_drop_off_window.description: GTFS specification requires both the start and end pickup/drop-off windows to be provided together, if used.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

endPickupDropOffWindow.description: The end pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

startPickupDropOffWindow.description: The start pickup drop off window of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, gives only one end of its pickup and drop-off window, the time span in which riders can be picked up or dropped off. Without both `start_pickup_drop_off_window` and `end_pickup_drop_off_window`, apps cannot tell when the service runs.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, fill in the empty end of the window, so both `start_pickup_drop_off_window` and `end_pickup_drop_off_window` have a time.
If the row is not meant to have a window, empty both and give it an arrival and departure time instead.

missing_prior_day_booking_field_value.summary: The `prior_notice_last_day` and the `prior_notice_last_time` values are required for prior day `booking_type` in booking_rules.txt.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) is for trips booked one or more days before (`booking_type` 2), but it has no deadline: no last day (`prior_notice_last_day`) and no time (`prior_notice_last_time`). Riders cannot tell when it is too late.

fix: Set `prior_notice_last_day` and `prior_notice_last_time` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}}, for example 1 and 17:00:00 for "by 5 pm the day before".
If riders can actually book the same day, set `booking_type` to 1 and give the notice in minutes in `prior_notice_duration_min`.

missing_prior_notice_duration_min.summary: `prior_notice_duration_min` value is required for same day `booking_type` in booking_rules.txt.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) is for trips booked earlier the same day (`booking_type` 1), but it does not say how many minutes before the trip riders must book (`prior_notice_duration_min`).

fix: Set `prior_notice_duration_min` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} to the minutes of notice riders must give, for example 60 for an hour.
If riders actually book one or more days before, set `booking_type` to 2 and give the deadline in `prior_notice_last_day` and `prior_notice_last_time`.

missing_prior_notice_last_day.summary: The `prior_notice_last_day` is required when booking_type=2 (prior day booking) is specified in booking_rules.txt.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) is for trips booked one or more days before (`booking_type` 2), but it does not say how many days ahead booking closes (`prior_notice_last_day`). Riders cannot tell when it is too late.

fix: Set `prior_notice_last_day` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} to the number of days before the trip that booking closes, for example 1 for the day before.
If riders can actually book the same day, set `booking_type` to 1 and give the notice in minutes in `prior_notice_duration_min`.

missing_prior_notice_last_time.summary: The `prior_notice_last_time` is required when booking_type=2 (prior day booking) is specified in booking_rules.txt.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) is for trips booked one or more days before (`booking_type` 2), but it does not say at what time booking closes (`prior_notice_last_time`). Riders cannot tell when it is too late.

fix: Set `prior_notice_last_time` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} to the time booking closes on the last day, for example 17:00:00 for 5 pm.
If riders can actually book the same day, set `booking_type` to 1 and give the notice in minutes in `prior_notice_duration_min`.

missing_prior_notice_start_time.summary: `prior_notice_start_time` value is required when `prior_notice_start_day` value is set in booking_rules.txt.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} (line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip) says booking opens {{priorNoticeStartDay|days}} before the trip (`prior_notice_start_day`), but not at what time that day (`prior_notice_start_time`). Apps cannot tell riders when they can first book.

fix: Set `prior_notice_start_time` for booking rule {{bookingRuleId}} to the time booking opens, for example 08:00:00 for 8 am.
If there is no earliest day to book, empty `prior_notice_start_day` instead.

missing_recommended_column.summary: A recommended column is missing in the input file.

fieldName.description: The name of the missing column.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: `{{filename}}` has no `{{fieldName}}` column. GTFS does not require it but recommends it, and apps show riders less without it.

fix: Add the `{{fieldName}}` column to `{{filename}}` and fill it in.

missing_recommended_field.description: The given field has no value in some input row, even though values are recommended.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

fieldName.description: The name of the missing field.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` leaves `{{fieldName}}` empty. GTFS does not require a value there but recommends one, and apps show riders less without it.

fix: Fill in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}`.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: The feed has no `{{filename}}`. GTFS does not require it but recommends it, and apps and data users rely on what it says.

fix: Add `{{filename}}` to the feed.
If the viewer lists `{{filename}}` but the validator did not find it, the files are probably in a folder inside the zip: zip the .txt files themselves, not their folder.

missing_required_agency_id.summary: Agency id is required when there are multiple agencies.
missing_required_agency_id.description: `agency.agency_id`, `routes.agency_id` or `fare_attributes.agency_id` is required when there are multiple agencies.

agencyName.description: The agency name if it can be obtained.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number in the source file where the error occurs.

filename.description: The name of the file where the error occurs.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` leaves `agency_id`, the id that says which agency a row belongs to, empty.
`agency.txt`, the list of agencies, has more than one agency. Then every agency needs an id, and every route and fare must name its agency, or apps cannot tell who runs it.

fix: Fill in `agency_id` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with an id from `agency.txt`.
If the row is in `agency.txt`, give that agency a short id of its own and use it in `routes.txt` for its routes.

missing_required_column.summary: A required column is missing in the input file.

fieldName.description: The name of the missing column.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: `{{filename}}` has no `{{fieldName}}` column, and GTFS requires one. Apps may reject the file, or the whole feed.

fix: Add the `{{fieldName}}` column to `{{filename}}` and fill it in for every row.
If the column is there under a slightly different name, correct the name in the header.

missing_required_element.summary: A required element is missing in `locations.geojson`.

featureId.description: The id of the faulty record.

featureIndex.description: Index of the feature in the feature collection.

steps.text: Zone {{featureId}} in `locations.geojson`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, lacks a part GTFS requires: `{{missingElement}}`. Apps may reject the zone, and with it the trips that serve it.

fix: Add `{{missingElement}}` to zone {{featureId}} in `locations.geojson`.
Every zone needs an `id`, a `type` of Feature, `properties` (which may be empty, written as {}) and a `geometry`.

missing_required_field.description: The given field has no value in some input row, even though values are required.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

fieldName.description: The name of the missing field.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` leaves `{{fieldName}}` empty, and GTFS requires a value there. Apps may skip the row, or reject the file.

fix: Fill in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}`.
Some columns are required only when another one is set; the card above says what makes `{{fieldName}}` required on this row.

missing_required_file.description: If this notice is triggered for every core file, it might be a problem with the input. To create a zip file from the GTFS `.txt` files: select all the `.txt` files, right-click, and compress. Do not compress the folder containing the files.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: The feed has no `{{filename}}`, one of the files every GTFS feed must have. Apps will reject the feed, or show riders nothing from it.

fix: Add `{{filename}}` to the feed.
If the viewer lists `{{filename}}` but the validator did not find it, the files are probably in a folder inside the zip: zip the .txt files themselves, not their folder.

missing_stop_name.summary: `stops.stop_name` is required for `location_type` equal to `0`, `1`, or `2`.
missing_stop_name.description: `stops.stop_name` is required for locations that are stops (`location_type=0`), stations (`location_type=1`) or entrances/exits (`location_type=2`).

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The `stops.stop_id` of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt`, the list of stops and stations, is a {{locationType|words}} with no `stop_name`. Stops, stations and entrances need a name: riders see it in apps, on screens and in announcements.

fix: Fill in `stop_name` for {{stopId}} on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt` with the name on the sign at the stop.
If the row is really a node inside a station or a boarding area, set `location_type` to 3 or 4, which may go without a name.

missing_stop_times_record.summary: Only one stop_times record is found where two are required.
missing_stop_times_record.description: Travel within the same location group or GeoJSON location requires two records in stop_times.txt with the same location_group_id or location_id.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} is a flex trip: it serves a zone or a time window, booked in advance, rather than fixed stops at fixed times. Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, lets riders travel within one zone or group of stops.
A ride within one area needs two rows: one where riders are picked up, one where they are dropped off. Trip {{tripId}} has only this one, so apps cannot work out where the ride may end.

fix: Add a second row to trip {{tripId}} in `stop_times.txt` for the same zone or group of stops, with the next `stop_sequence`.
Use the first row for pickups (`drop_off_type` 1) and the second for drop-offs (`pickup_type` 1).

missing_timepoint_value.summary: `stop_times.timepoint` value is missing for a record.
missing_timepoint_value.description: When at least one of `stop_times.arrival_time` or `stop_times.departure_time` are provided, `stop_times.timepoint` should be defined

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Stop {{stopSequence}} of trip {{tripId}} has a time, but its `timepoint` is empty. `timepoint` says whether that time is exact (1) or an estimate (0).
The trip in its timetable. Left empty, apps take every time as exact; if some are estimates, riders expect the vehicle at a time it does not keep.

fix: Set `timepoint` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt` to 1 if the vehicle is scheduled to be there at that time, or to 0 if the time is an estimate.
Fill in `timepoint` for every other stop of trip {{tripId}} that has a time.

missing_trip_edge.description: First and last stop of a trip must define both `arrival_time` and `departure_time` fields. Per [stop_times.txt](http://gtfs.org/reference/static/#stop_timestxt), "If there are not separate times for arrival and departure at a stop, enter the same value for arrival_time and departure_time."

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

steps.text: Stop {{stopSequence}} is where trip {{tripId}} starts or ends, and it has no `{{specifiedField}}`. The first and last stops of a trip must have both an arrival and a departure time.
The trip in its timetable, with a gap at one end. Apps cannot say when the trip starts or ends, and may drop it from journey plans.

fix: Fill in `{{specifiedField}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`; if the vehicle does not wait there, use the same time for `arrival_time` and `departure_time`.
If the trip really starts or ends at another stop, add that stop to the trip with both times.

mixed_case_recommended_field.summary: This field has customer-facing text and should use Mixed Case (should contain upper and lower case letters).
mixed_case_recommended_field.description:
This field contains customer-facing text and should use Mixed Case (upper and lower case letters) to ensure good readability when displayed to riders. Avoid the use of abbreviations throughout the feed (e.g. St. for Street) unless a location is called by its abbreviated name (e.g. “JFK Airport”). Abbreviations may be problematic for accessibility by screen reader software and voice user interfaces.

Good examples:

Field Text | Dataset
"Schwerin, Hauptbahnhof" | Verkehrsverbund Berlin-Brandenburg
"Red Hook/Atlantic Basin" | NYC Ferry
"Campo Grande Norte" | Carris

Bad examples:

Field Text

"GALLERIA MALL"

"3427 GG 17"

"21 Clark Rd Est"

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

filename.description: Name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value "{{fieldValue}}", with no mix of capital and small letters. Riders read this text in apps and on signs.
Text in capitals only is harder to read, and screen readers may spell it out letter by letter. Names read best with capitals only where they belong.

fix: Rewrite "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with capitals only where they belong, as in "Market Street".
Keep capitals for names that are really written that way, such as JFK Airport, and spell out abbreviations such as St. for Street.

more_than_one_entity.summary: More than one row in CSV.
more_than_one_entity.description: The file is expected to have a single entity but has more (e.g., "feed_info.txt").

filename.description: Name of the faulty file.

steps.text: `{{filename}}` has {{entityCount}} rows, but it should have one: it describes the feed as a whole. Apps read only one row, and may pick the wrong one.

fix: Keep the one row of `{{filename}}` that is correct and delete the others.

new_line_in_value.summary: New line or carriage return in a value in CSV file.
new_line_in_value.description:
This error is usually found when the CSV file does not close double quotes properly, so the next line is considered as a continuation of the previous line.

Example: the following file was intended to have fields "f11", "f12", "f21", "f22", but it actually parses as two fields: "f11", "f12\nf21,\"f22\"".

``` f11,"f12 f21,"f22" ```

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

fieldName.description: The name of the faulty field.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: The `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` has a line break inside it. Many apps read one row per line, so they split this row in two.

fix: Replace the line break in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with a space.
If the break comes from a double quote that was never closed, close it where the value ends.

non_ascii_or_non_printable_char.summary: Non ascii or non printable char in ID field.
non_ascii_or_non_printable_char.description: A value of a field with type ID contains non ASCII or non printable characters. This is not recommended.

columnName.description: Name of the column where the error occurred.

csvRowNumber.description: Row number of the faulty record.

filename.description: Name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` has the id "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{columnName}}`, and it contains a character outside plain letters, digits and punctuation: an accented letter, a symbol or an invisible character. The marks below show which.
Riders never see ids, but other files and systems match on them. A character like this can be saved or typed differently elsewhere, and then the ids no longer match.

fix: Change the id "{{fieldValue}}" in `{{columnName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` to use only plain letters (A to Z), digits, - and _, for example É becomes E.
Change it everywhere else the feed uses this id too, such as in `stop_times.txt` for a stop, so the files still match.

number_out_of_range.description: The values in the given column of the input rows are out of range.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

fieldName.description: The name of the faulty field.

fieldType.description: The type of the faulty field.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value {{fieldValue|round}}, but it must be a {{fieldType}}. Apps cannot use a value outside that range, and may drop the row or reject the feed.
A value just outside the range is often a typing slip or two columns swapped, such as a latitude and a longitude.

fix: Correct `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` to a value that is a {{fieldType}}.
If the other values on the line look swapped too, put each back in its own column.

overlapping_frequency.description: Trip frequencies must not overlap in time. Two entries X and Y are considered to directly overlap if X.start_time is less than or equal to Y.start_time and Y.start_time is less than X.end_time.

prevCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the first frequency.

tripId.description: The trip id associated to the first frequency.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} is in `frequencies.txt`, trips described as "every N minutes" between two times. Line {{prevCsvRowNumber}} runs it until {{prevEndTime}}, but line {{currCsvRowNumber}} starts again at {{currStartTime}}.
From {{currStartTime}} to {{prevEndTime}} both periods apply. Apps count two sets of departures and show the service running more often than it does.

fix: Set `start_time` on line {{currCsvRowNumber}} to {{prevEndTime}}, or `end_time` on line {{prevCsvRowNumber}} to {{currStartTime}}, so one period ends where the next starts.
If lines {{prevCsvRowNumber}} and {{currCsvRowNumber}} describe the same service, merge them into one row.

overlapping_zone_and_pickup_drop_off_win.summary: Two entities have overlapping pickup/drop-off windows and zones.
overlapping_zone_and_pickup_drop_off_win.description: Two entities in `stop_times.txt` with the same `trip_id` have the same `pickup_type` or `drop_off_type`, overlapping pickup/drop-off windows and overlapping zones in `locations.geojson`.

endPickupDropOffWindow1.description: The `end_pickup_drop_off_window` of the first entity in `stop_times.txt`.

endPickupDropOffWindow2.description: The `end_pickup_drop_off_window` of the second entity in `stop_times.txt`.

startPickupDropOffWindow1.description: The `start_pickup_drop_off_window` of the first entity in `stop_times.txt`.

startPickupDropOffWindow2.description: The `start_pickup_drop_off_window` of the second entity in `stop_times.txt`.

stopSequence1.description: The `stop_sequence` of the first entity in `stop_times.txt`.

stopSequence2.description: The `stop_sequence` of the second entity in `stop_times.txt`.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} is a flex trip: it serves a zone or a time window, booked in advance, rather than fixed stops at fixed times. Two of its rows in `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, serve zones {{locationId1}} and {{locationId2}}, and the zones overlap.

Their times overlap too: {{startPickupDropOffWindow1}} to {{endPickupDropOffWindow1}}, and {{startPickupDropOffWindow2}} to {{endPickupDropOffWindow2}}. Both rows allow the same kind of pickup or drop-off, so a rider in the shared area at the shared time matches both, and apps cannot tell which one applies.

fix: Redraw zones {{locationId1}} and {{locationId2}} in `locations.geojson` so they no longer overlap, or change the windows of trip {{tripId}} so they no longer share any time.
If both rows describe the same service, merge them into one row with one zone and one window.

pathway_dangling_generic_node.summary: A generic node has only one incident location in a pathway graph.
pathway_dangling_generic_node.description: Such generic node is useless because there is no benefit in visiting it.

csvRowNumber.description: Row number of the dangling generic node.

parentStation.description: The parent station of the dangling generic node.

stopId.description: The id of the dangling generic node.

stopName.description: The stop name of the dangling generic node.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) is a node inside station {{parentStation}}: a point where walkways meet. It is joined to only one other place, so it leads nowhere.
`pathways.txt` lists the walkways, stairs and elevators in stations. Only one of them touches {{stopId}}. A node helps where paths meet or turn; a dead end adds nothing to the directions apps give.

fix: If {{stopId}} is a real junction, add the pathways that leave it, so it joins at least two other places.
If {{stopId}} is only a point along one walkway, delete it and connect the pathway straight to the places at both ends.

pathway_loop.summary: A pathway starts and ends at the same location.
pathway_loop.description: A pathway should not have same values for `from_stop_id` and `to_stop_id`.

csvRowNumber.description: Row number of the faulty row from `pathways.txt`.

pathwayId.description: The id of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The `pathway.stop_id` that is repeated in `pathways.from_stop_id` and `pathways.to_stop_id`.

steps.text: Pathway {{pathwayId}}, line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`, the walkways and stairs inside stations, starts and ends at the same place, {{stopId}}. A path that goes nowhere cannot help a rider through the station.
This is {{stopId}} in `stops.txt`. The pathway was probably meant to lead from here to another place in the same station.

fix: Change one end of pathway {{pathwayId}} to the place at the other end of the walkway.
If the pathway is a mistake, delete line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`.

pathway_to_platform_with_boarding_areas.summary: A pathway has an endpoint that is a platform which has boarding areas.
pathway_to_platform_with_boarding_areas.description: A platform that has boarding areas is treated as a parent object, not a point. In such cases, the platform must not have pathways assigned - instead, pathways must be assigned to its boarding areas.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty row.

pathwayId.description: The id of the faulty pathway.

stopId.description: The id of the endpoint platform.

steps.text: Pathway {{pathwayId}}, line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`, leads to platform {{stopId}}. But that platform is divided into boarding areas: the parts where riders wait for a given door or car.
These are the boarding areas of {{stopId}} in `stops.txt`. Once a platform has them, pathways must lead to the boarding areas, so apps can guide riders to the right part of the platform.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`, change `{{fieldName}}` from {{stopId}} to the boarding area the walkway reaches.
If the walkway reaches several boarding areas, add a pathway to each of them.

pathway_to_stop_with_access_outside_of_s.summary: A pathway has an endpoint that is a stop with stop_access=1, which should be accessible outside of the station’s pathways.
pathway_to_stop_with_access_outside_of_s.description: Stops with stop_access=1 should not have pathways that link to them since they can be accessed from the street and are independent of the pathways inside the station.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

pathwayId.description: The pathway_id of the pathway record that triggered this notice.

platformCode.description: The platform code (if available) associated with the stop referenced by this pathway.

stopId.description: The stop_id (either from_stop_id or to_stop_id) that has stop_access == 1.

steps.text: Pathway {{pathwayId}}, line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`, the walkways inside stations, leads to {{stopId}}. But {{stopId}} says riders reach it straight from the street.
In `stops.txt`, `stop_access` 1 means reached from the street, not through the station. The pathway says the opposite, so apps cannot tell how riders get there.

fix: If riders reach {{stopId}} through the station, set its `stop_access` to 0 in `stops.txt`.
If riders reach {{stopId}} from the street, delete pathway {{pathwayId}} from `pathways.txt`.

pathway_to_wrong_location_type.summary: A pathway has an endpoint that is a station.
pathway_to_wrong_location_type.description: Pathways endpoints must be platforms (stops), entrances/exits, generic nodes or boarding areas.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty row.

pathwayId.description: The id of the faulty pathway.

stopId.description: The id of the endpoint station.

steps.text: Pathway {{pathwayId}}, line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`, leads to {{stopId}}, which is a whole station. A pathway is one walkway or flight of stairs, so both its ends must be places inside the station.

`location_type` is the kind of place: 0 a stop or platform, 1 a station, 2 an entrance, 3 a node inside a station, 4 a boarding area. {{stopId}} is a 1. A pathway may end at any of these but a station.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `pathways.txt`, change `{{fieldName}}` to the platform, entrance, node or boarding area the walkway really reaches.
If that place is not in `stops.txt` yet, add it with {{stopId}} as its `parent_station`.

pathway_unreachable_location.summary: A location is not reachable at least in one direction: from the entrances or to the exits.
pathway_unreachable_location.description:
Notices are reported for platforms, boarding areas and generic nodes but not for entrances or stations.

Notices are not reported for platforms that have boarding areas since such platforms may not have incident pathways. Instead, notices are reported for the boarding areas.

csvRowNumber.description: Row number of the unreachable location.

hasEntrance.description: Whether the location is reachable from entrances.

hasExit.description: Whether some exit can be reached from the location.

locationType.description: The type of the unreachable location.

parentStation.description: The parent of the unreachable location.

stopId.description: The id of the unreachable location.

stopName.description: The stop name of the unreachable location.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}), in station {{parentStation}}, is cut off: following the station's walkways, a rider cannot get to it from an entrance, or out of it to an exit.
Reachable from an entrance: {{hasEntrance|yesno}}. Leads to an exit: {{hasExit|yesno}}. These are the station's walkways in `pathways.txt`; a one-way one can only be walked in one direction.

fix: Add the pathways that connect {{stopId}} to the rest of {{parentStation}}, from an entrance to it and from it back to an exit.
Check that the one-way pathways point the right way, since one the wrong way round cuts a place off.

platform_without_parent_station.summary: A platform has no `parent_station` field set.
platform_without_parent_station.description: This is different from `location_without_parent_station` since it is less severe.

csvRowNumber.description: Row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty record.

stopName.description: The stop name of the faulty record.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) has a `platform_code`, the number or letter of a platform. But its `parent_station` is empty, so it does not say which station it is part of.
These are the stations in `stops.txt`. Apps group a station's platforms under its name; if {{stopName}} belongs to one of these, riders see it as a stop on its own.

fix: If {{stopName}} is part of a station, set its `parent_station` to that station's `stop_id`.
If {{stopName}} is a stop on its own, there is nothing to fix.

point_near_origin.summary: A point is too close to origin `(0, 0)`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty row.

entityId.description: The id of the faulty entity.

featureIndex.description: The index of the feature in the feature collection.

filename.description: The name of the affected GTFS file.

latFieldName.description: The name of the field that uses latitude value.

latFieldValue.description: The latitude of the faulty row.

lonFieldName.description: The name of the field that uses longitude value.

lonFieldValue.description: The longitude of the faulty row

steps.text: A place in `{{filename}}` is at {{latFieldValue|coord}}, {{lonFieldValue|coord}}, close to latitude 0, longitude 0, in the ocean off West Africa. That is almost always a coordinate left at zero, not a real position.
It is part of {{entityId}}, an area riders can be picked up or dropped off in. With a point out at sea, apps would stretch the area across the ocean, or not show it.

fix: Correct the coordinates of this place in `{{filename}}` to where it really is.
Look for a 0 left in the latitude or longitude, or the two swapped: they are the usual cause.

point_near_pole.summary: A point is too close to the North or South Pole.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty row.

entityId.description: The id of the faulty entity.

featureIndex.description: The index of the feature in the feature collection.

filename.description: The name of the affected GTFS file.

latFieldName.description: The name of the field that uses latitude value.

latFieldValue.description: The latitude of the faulty row.

lonFieldName.description: The name of the field that uses longitude value.

lonFieldValue.description: The longitude of the faulty row

steps.text: A place in `{{filename}}` is at {{latFieldValue|coord}}, {{lonFieldValue|coord}}, within a degree of the North or South Pole. No transit runs there, so the latitude is almost certainly wrong.
It is part of {{entityId}}, an area riders can be picked up or dropped off in. With a point at the pole, apps would stretch the area across half the globe, or not show it.

fix: Correct the coordinates of this place in `{{filename}}` to where it really is.
Look for latitude and longitude swapped, or a wrong sign: they are the usual cause.

prior_notice_last_day_after_start_day.summary: Prior notice last day should not be greater than the prior notice start day in booking_rules.txt.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

priorNoticeLastDay.description: The value of the `prior_notice_last_day` of the faulty field.

priorNoticeStartDay.description: The value of the `prior_notice_start_day` of the faulty field.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `booking_rules.txt`, how and when riders must book a trip, opens booking {{priorNoticeStartDay|days}} before the trip (`prior_notice_start_day`) but closes it {{priorNoticeLastDay|days}} before (`prior_notice_last_day`). Booking closes before it opens, so riders can never book.

fix: If the two were entered the wrong way round, set `prior_notice_start_day` to {{priorNoticeLastDay}} and `prior_notice_last_day` to {{priorNoticeStartDay}} on line {{csvRowNumber}}.
Otherwise, make `prior_notice_start_day` at least {{priorNoticeLastDay}}, so booking opens on or before the day it closes.

route_both_short_and_long_name_missing.summary: Both `route_short_name` and `route_long_name` are missing for a route.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

routeId.description: The id of the faulty record.

steps.text: Route {{routeId}} has no name: in `routes.txt`, both `route_short_name`, the number riders know it by, and `route_long_name`, its full name, are empty. Apps have nothing to show riders, and some reject the feed.

fix: Give route {{routeId}} a `route_short_name` (the number riders know it by), a `route_long_name`, or both.

route_color_contrast.description: A route's color and `route_text_color` should be contrasting.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

routeColor.description: The faulty record's HTML route color.

routeId.description: The id of the faulty record.

routeTextColor.description: The faulty record's HTML route text color.

steps.text: Route {{routeId}}'s label has {{routeTextColor}} text on {{routeColor}}, hard to read for riders with low vision or in bright sun. In `routes.txt`, `route_color` is the colour apps draw the route in and `route_text_color` the colour of the text on its label.

fix: Change `route_text_color` of route {{routeId}} to a colour that stands out on {{routeColor}}: black (000000) on a light colour, white (FFFFFF) on a dark one.
If the text colour has to stay, make `route_color` darker or lighter so the text reads on it.

route_long_name_contains_short_name.summary: Long name should not contain short name for a single route.
route_long_name_contains_short_name.description:
In routes.txt, `route_long_name` should not contain the value for `route_short_name`, because when both are provided, they are often combined by transit applications. Note that only one of the two fields is required. If there is no short name used for a route, use `route_long_name` only.

Good examples:

route_short_name/route_long_name | Dataset
"N"/"Judah" | Muni San Fransisco
"6"/"ML King Jr Blvd" | Trimet Portland Streetcar
"55"/"Boulevard Saint Laurent" | STM Montreal
"1"/"Rangiora/Cashmere" | Metro Christchurch

Bad examples:

route_short_name/route_long_name

"604"/"604"

"14"/"Route 14"

"2"/"Route 2: Bellows Falls In-Town"

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

routeId.description: The id of the faulty record.

steps.text: Route {{routeId}} is numbered {{routeShortName}} in `route_short_name`, and its name in `route_long_name`, {{routeLongName}}, repeats the number. Apps usually show the two together, so riders read "{{routeShortName}} {{routeLongName}}".

fix: Take {{routeShortName}} out of `route_long_name` of route {{routeId}}, keeping only the name.
If the route has no number, leave `route_short_name` empty and keep only `route_long_name`.

route_networks_specified_in_more_than_on.summary: Indicates that route network identifiers are specified across multiple files.
route_networks_specified_in_more_than_on.description: This notice highlights a data integrity issue where route network specifications are redundantly defined in more than one file. According to specifications, a route network identifier should be uniquely defined in a single file. Any additional definitions of route network specifications in other files are considered conditionally forbidden.

fieldName.description: Name of the field in fileNameA

fileNameA.description: The name of the first file.

fileNameB.description: The name of the second file which presence duplicates route networks specification.

steps.text: This feed describes its route networks, groups of routes often used for fares, in two ways at once: the `{{fieldName}}` column of `{{fileNameA}}` and the file `{{fileNameB}}`. Only one way is allowed.

`{{fileNameB}}`, the other way: `networks.txt` names the networks and `route_networks.txt` puts routes in them. When the two ways disagree, apps cannot tell which is right and may charge the wrong fare.

fix: Keep one way. To keep the network files, remove the `network_id` column from `routes.txt`.
To keep `network_id` in `routes.txt` instead, remove `networks.txt` and `route_networks.txt`.

route_short_name_too_long.summary: Short name of a route is too long (more than 12 characters).

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

routeId.description: The id of the faulty record.

steps.text: Route {{routeId}}'s short name, {{routeShortName}}, is longer than 12 characters. `route_short_name` in `routes.txt` is the number or code riders see on the vehicle and in an app's badge, like 10 or N; a long one gets cut off.

fix: Move {{routeShortName}} to `route_long_name` of route {{routeId}}, and give `route_short_name` a short code or leave it empty.

runtime_exception_in_loader_error.summary: RuntimeException while loading GTFS dataset in memory.
runtime_exception_in_loader_error.description: A [RuntimeException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/RuntimeException.html) occurred while loading a table. This normally indicates a bug in validator.

filename.description: The name of the file that caused the exception.

message.description: The error message that explains the reason for the exception.

steps.text: This is most likely not a problem in the feed's data: the validator itself failed while reading `{{filename}}`, so that file was not checked.

fix: Run the validator again.
If it happens again, report it to the gtfs-validator project on GitHub, with the message above, the error name {{exception}} and, if you can, `{{filename}}`.

runtime_exception_in_validator_error.description: A [RuntimeException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/RuntimeException.html) occurred during validation. This normally indicates a bug in validator code, e.g., in a custom validator class.

message.description: The error message that explains the reason for the exception.

validator.description: The name of the validator that caused the exception.

steps.text: This is not a finding about the feed: one of the validator's own checks failed, so what it checks was not checked. An unusual value in the feed can set it off, and the message may name it.

fix: Run the validator again, and if the message names a value, such as a date, check that value in the feed.
If it happens again, report it to the gtfs-validator project on GitHub, with the message above and the name of the check, {{validator}}.

same_name_and_description_for_route.summary: Same name and description for route.
same_name_and_description_for_route.description:
The GTFS spec defines `routes.txt` [route_desc](https://gtfs.org/reference/static/#routestxt) as:

Description of a route that provides useful, quality information. Do not simply duplicate the name of the route.

See the GTFS and GTFS Best Practices links below for more examples of how to populate the `route_short_name`, `route_long_name`, and `route_desc` fields.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

routeId.description: The id of the faulty record.

steps.text: Route {{routeId}}'s description, {{routeDesc}}, only repeats its name in `{{specifiedField}}`. In `routes.txt`, `route_desc` should tell riders more, such as where the route goes or when it runs; a copy of the name tells them nothing.

fix: Write a real description in `route_desc` of route {{routeId}}, such as where it goes and when it runs.
If there is nothing more to say, leave `route_desc` empty.

same_name_and_description_for_stop.summary: Same name and description for stop.
same_name_and_description_for_stop.description:
The GTFS spec defines `stops.txt` [stop_description](https://gtfs.org/reference/static/#stopstxt) as:

Description of the location that provides useful, quality information. Do not simply duplicate the name of the location.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty record.

steps.text: Stop {{stopId}} has the same name and description: both are "{{stopDesc}}". `stop_desc`, the description, should tell riders something the name does not, such as which side of the street the stop is on.

fix: Write a `stop_desc` for {{stopId}} that adds something, such as "North side of Main Street, by the library", or leave it empty.

same_route_and_agency_url.description: A route should not have the same `routes.route_url` as a record from `agency.txt`.

agencyCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `agency.txt`.

agencyName.description: The faulty record's referenced agency name.

routeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `routes.txt`.

steps.text: Route {{routeId}}'s web page is {{routeUrl}}. In `routes.txt`, `route_url` should lead to a page about this route: its map, timetable and service changes.
That is the home page of {{agencyName}}, as `agency.txt`, the list of agencies, gives it. A rider who taps the route's link lands there and has to look for the route.

fix: Set `route_url` of route {{routeId}} to the page about this route on the agency's site.
If there is no such page, leave `route_url` empty: apps then link to {{routeUrl}} through the agency.

same_stop_and_agency_url.description: A stop should not have the same `stops.stop_url` as a record from `agency.txt`.

agencyCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `agency.txt`.

stopCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `stops.txt`.

stopId.description: The faulty record's id.

steps.text: Stop {{stopId}} links to {{stopUrl}}, the same web page as the agency {{agencyName}}. `stop_url` should be a page about this stop: its departures, its map, how accessible it is.
This is {{agencyName}} in `agency.txt`, with the same address in `agency_url`. A rider who taps the stop's link lands on the agency's home page instead.

fix: Set `stop_url` of {{stopId}} to a page about that stop, or leave it empty if there is none.

same_stop_and_route_url.description: A stop should not have the same `stop.stop_url` as a record from `routes.txt`.

routeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `routes.txt`.

stopCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `stops.txt`.

stopId.description: The faulty record's id.

steps.text: Stop {{stopId}} links to {{stopUrl}}, the same web page as route {{routeId}}. `stop_url` should be a page about this stop: its departures, its map, how accessible it is.
This is route {{routeId}} in `routes.txt`, with the same address in `route_url`. A rider who taps the stop's link lands on the route's page instead.

fix: Set `stop_url` of {{stopId}} to a page about that stop, or leave it empty if there is none.

service_extends_far_in_the_future.summary: A service end date is more than 2 years in the future.

serviceId.description: The service_id that ends far in the future.

serviceWindowEndDate.description: The end date of the service (YYYY-MM-DD format).

steps.text: Service {{serviceId}} still has trips on {{serviceWindowEndDate|date}}, more than two years ahead. Schedules are rarely known that far out, so the date is often a placeholder or a typo.
Service days, opened on {{serviceWindowEndDate|date}}, the last day {{serviceId}} runs. Riders planning that far ahead would see trips that may never run.

fix: If the schedule is not confirmed that far ahead, set `end_date` for service {{serviceId}} to the last day it is known to run.
If it really is planned until {{serviceWindowEndDate|date}}, nothing needs to change.

service_has_no_active_day_of_the_week.summary: A service is not valid for any day of the week.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number in calendar.txt where the error occurs.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `calendar.txt`, the weekly pattern of days each service runs, marks service {{serviceId}} for no day of the week: `monday` to `sunday` are all 0.
Its trips then run only on single days added in `calendar_dates.txt`, if there are any. If {{serviceId}} should run every week, riders will not see its trips.

fix: Set the weekdays service {{serviceId}} runs to 1 on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `calendar.txt`.
If it only runs on single days, remove its row from `calendar.txt` and list those days in `calendar_dates.txt` with `exception_type` 1.

service_window_outside_feed_period.summary: A service window is not covered by the feed's validity period.

daysAfterFeedEnd.description: Number of days the service window extends after feed_end_date (0 if none).

daysBeforeFeedStart.description: Number of days the service window extends before feed_start_date (0 if none).

serviceId.description: The service_id whose active window extends outside the feed validity period.

serviceWindowEndDate.description: The last active date of the service window.

serviceWindowStartDate.description: The first active date of the service window.

steps.text: Service {{serviceId}} runs from {{serviceWindowStartDate|date}} to {{serviceWindowEndDate|date}}, partly outside the period the feed says it is valid for. It runs {{daysBeforeFeedStart|days}} before that period starts and {{daysAfterFeedEnd|days}} after it ends.
That period is `feed_start_date` to `feed_end_date` in `feed_info.txt`, the feed's description of itself. Apps may ignore the service outside it, or treat the feed as out of date.

fix: If service {{serviceId}} really runs until {{serviceWindowEndDate|date}}, widen `feed_start_date` and `feed_end_date` in `feed_info.txt` to cover it.
If the feed period is right, shorten the service's dates in `calendar.txt`, or remove its days outside the period from `calendar_dates.txt`.

single_shape_point.summary: The shape within `shapes.txt` contains a single shape point.
single_shape_point.description: A shape should contain more than one shape point to visualize the route

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Shape {{shapeId}} has a single point, on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `shapes.txt`, the file of lines trips are drawn with on a map. One point cannot make a line, so there is nothing to draw.
These trips are drawn with shape {{shapeId}}. Apps show them with no line on the map, or with straight lines from stop to stop.

fix: Add the points that trace the way shape {{shapeId}} goes, from its first stop to its last.
If the trips should not have a line, remove shape {{shapeId}} and clear `shape_id` on its trips in `trips.txt`.

start_and_end_range_equal.summary: Two date or time fields are equal.
start_and_end_range_equal.description: The fields `frequencies.start_date` and `frequencies.end_date` have been found equal in `frequencies.txt`. The GTFS spec is currently unclear how this case should be handled (e.g., is it a trip that circulates once?). It is recommended to use a trip not defined via frequencies.txt for this case.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

entityId.description: The id of the faulty entity.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}`, `{{startFieldName}}` and `{{endFieldName}}` are both {{value}}. The period this row describes has no length.

`frequencies.txt` lists trips that repeat every few minutes, from a start time to an end time. With no time in between, GTFS does not say whether this trip runs once or not at all, so apps may disagree.

fix: If the trip runs only once, at {{value}}, remove line {{csvRowNumber}} from `{{filename}}` and give the trip its own times in `stop_times.txt`.
If the trip repeats over a period, set `{{endFieldName}}` to the time that period ends.

start_and_end_range_out_of_order.summary: Two date or time fields are out of order.
start_and_end_range_out_of_order.description: Date or time fields have been found out of order in `calendar.txt`, `feed_info.txt` and `stop_times.txt`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}`, `{{endFieldName}}` ({{endValue|date}}) comes before `{{startFieldName}}` ({{startValue|date}}). The period this row describes ends before it begins.
Apps cannot run a service or a trip over a period that goes backwards. They may drop it, and riders then do not see it at all.

fix: If the two values were entered the wrong way round, swap `{{startFieldName}}` and `{{endFieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}`.
If only one of them is wrong, correct that one so the period ends after it starts.

station_with_parent_station.description: Field `parent_station` must be empty when `location_type` is 1.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty record.

stopName.description: The stops.stop_name of the faulty record.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) is a station, yet its `parent_station` says it is part of {{parentStation}}. Platforms and entrances belong to a station, but a station belongs to nothing.
This is {{parentStation}}, the place it names. If {{stopName}} is really part of it, such as a hall or an entrance, it should not be a station itself.

fix: If {{stopName}} is a station of its own, empty its `parent_station` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt`.
If {{stopName}} is part of {{parentStation}}, change its `location_type` to 0 for a platform, 2 for an entrance or 3 for a point inside the station.

stop_access_specified_for_incorrect_loca.summary: A location that is not a stop has stop_access specified.
stop_access_specified_for_incorrect_loca.description: Stops.stop_access is forbidden for locations that are stations, entrances, generic nodes or boarding areas. It can only be specific when a stop is associated with a parent station.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The `stops.stop_id` of the faulty record.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) is a {{locationType|words}}, yet its `stop_access` says "{{stopAccess|words}}". `stop_access` says how riders reach a platform, from the street or through its station, so only platforms may have it.

`location_type` is the kind of place: 0 a stop or platform, 1 a station, 2 an entrance, 3 a node inside a station, 4 a boarding area. On anything but a 0 inside a station, apps cannot make sense of `stop_access`.

fix: Empty `stop_access` for {{stopId}} on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt`.
If {{stopId}} is really a platform, set its `location_type` to 0 and its `parent_station` to its station, and keep `stop_access`.

stop_access_specified_for_stop_with_no_p.summary: A stop without a value for parent station has stop_access specified.
stop_access_specified_for_stop_with_no_p.description: stops.stop_access is forbidden for stops that are not associated with a parent station.

csvRowNumber.description: The row of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The `stops.stop_id` of the faulty record.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) says "{{stopAccess|words}}" in `stop_access`, but its `parent_station` is empty, so it is not part of a station. `stop_access` only says how riders reach a platform inside a station.

fix: If {{stopName}} is a stop on the street, empty its `stop_access` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt`.
If {{stopName}} is a platform of a station, set its `parent_station` to that station's `stop_id` and keep `stop_access`.

stop_has_too_many_matches_for_shape.summary: Stop entry that has many potential matches to the trip's path of travel, as defined by the shape entry in `shapes.txt`.
stop_has_too_many_matches_for_shape.description: This potentially indicates a problem with the location of the stop or the path of the shape.

match.description: Latitude and longitude pair of the location.

matchCount.description: The number of matches for the stop that is referred to.

shapeId.description: The id of the shape that is referred to.

stopId.description: The id of the stop that is referred to.

stopName.description: The name of the stop that is referred to.

stopTimeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `stop_times.txt`.

tripCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `trips.txt`.

tripId.description: The id of the trip that is referred to.

steps.text: Shape {{shapeId}}, the line trip {{tripId}} is drawn with, passes close to {{stopName}} {{matchCount}} times. An app cannot tell at which pass the vehicle stops.
{{stopName}} among the trip's stops, numbered in order. Look for where the line loops or zigzags near it: apps following the vehicle may show it in the wrong place.

fix: If shape {{shapeId}} loops or zigzags near {{stopName}} by mistake, redraw it so it passes the stop only as often as the trip does.
If the stop is in the wrong place, correct `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` for {{stopId}} in `stops.txt`.
If the trip really passes {{stopName}} several times, add `shape_dist_traveled` to `stop_times.txt` and `shapes.txt` so apps know which pass is meant.

stop_time_timepoint_without_times.description: Any records with `stop_times.timepoint` set to 1 must define a value for `stop_times.arrival_time` and `stop_times.departure_time` fields.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Stop {{stopSequence}} of trip {{tripId}} is marked as a `timepoint`, a stop with an exact scheduled time, but its `{{specifiedField}}` is empty.
The trip in its timetable. Apps are told the time there is exact, yet there is no time to show, so they may reject the trip.

fix: Fill in `{{specifiedField}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`.
If the vehicle has no exact time there, leave both times empty and set `timepoint` to 0; apps then estimate the time.

stop_time_with_arrival_before_previous_d.summary: Backwards time travel between stops in `stop_times.txt`
stop_time_with_arrival_before_previous_d.description: For a given `trip_id`, the `arrival_time` of (n+1)-th stoptime in sequence must not precede the `departure_time` of n-th stoptime in sequence in `stop_times.txt`.

arrivalTime.description: Arrival time at the faulty record.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

departureTime.description: Departure time at the previous stop time.

prevCsvRowNumber.description: The row of the previous stop time.

tripId.description: The trip_id associated to the faulty record.

steps.text: On trip {{tripId}}, the vehicle leaves a stop at {{departureTime}} and reaches the next one at {{arrivalTime}}, before it has left.
Played at its scheduled pace, the trip goes back in time on that leg. Apps cannot show such a timetable, and journey planners may drop the trip.

fix: Correct `arrival_time` on line {{csvRowNumber}} or `departure_time` on line {{prevCsvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, so the vehicle arrives at {{departureTime}} or later.
Check `stop_sequence` too, since two stops listed in the wrong order look the same.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopSequence.description: The sequence of the faulty stop.

tripId.description: The trip_id associated to the faulty record.

steps.text: Stop {{stopSequence}} of trip {{tripId}} has only one of its two times: `{{specifiedField}}` is filled in, the other is empty. A stop must have both times, or neither.
The trip in its timetable. With one time missing, apps cannot tell when the vehicle arrives or leaves, and may drop the stop or the whole trip.

fix: Fill in the empty time on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`; if the vehicle does not wait at the stop, copy the `{{specifiedField}}` value into it.
If the time there is not known, leave both times empty and set `timepoint` to 0, so apps estimate it.

stop_too_far_from_shape.summary: Stop too far from trip shape.
stop_too_far_from_shape.description: Per GTFS Best Practices, route alignments (in `shapes.txt`) should be within 100 meters of stop locations which a trip serves. This potentially indicates a problem with the location of the stop or the path of the shape.

match.description: Latitude and longitude pair of the location.

shapeId.description: The id of the shape that is referred to.

stopId.description: The id of the stop that is referred to.

stopName.description: The name of the stop that is referred to.

stopTimeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `stop_times.txt`.

tripCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `trips.txt`.

tripId.description: The id of the trip that is referred to.

steps.text: {{stopName}} is {{geoDistanceToShape|m}} from shape {{shapeId}}, the line trip {{tripId}} is drawn with. Stops should be within 100 m of it, or apps show the vehicle passing far from where riders wait.
{{stopName}} among the stops of trip {{tripId}} in `stop_times.txt`, the timetable: one row per stop each trip makes. The map numbers them in order.
In `trips.txt`, the list of trips, `shape_id` says which line the trip is drawn with. If it should follow another line, this is the value to change.

fix: If the stop is in the wrong place, correct `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` for {{stopId}} in `stops.txt`.
If the line is wrong, redraw shape {{shapeId}} so it passes within 100 m of {{stopName}}, or give trip {{tripId}} a different `shape_id`.
If the vehicle really leaves the line to serve this stop, add the detour to shape {{shapeId}}.

stop_too_far_from_shape_using_user_dista.summary: Stop time too far from shape.
stop_too_far_from_shape_using_user_dista.description: A stop time entry that is a large distance away from the location of the shape in `shapes.txt` as defined by `shape_dist_traveled` values.

match.description: Latitude and longitude pair of the location.

shapeId.description: The id of the shape that is referred to.

stopId.description: The id of the stop that is referred to.

stopName.description: The name of the stop that is referred to.

stopTimeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `stop_times.txt`.

tripCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `trips.txt`.

tripId.description: The id of the trip that is referred to.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} gives {{stopName}} a distance along its line, shape {{shapeId}}. The point of the line at that distance is {{geoDistanceToShape|m}} from the stop itself.
The points of shape {{shapeId}}, each with its own `shape_dist_traveled`. The trip's distances must be measured the same way, or apps place the vehicle in the wrong spot.

fix: Correct `shape_dist_traveled` on line {{stopTimeCsvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt` to the distance along shape {{shapeId}} where {{stopName}} is.
Check that `stop_times.txt` and `shapes.txt` use the same unit, since metres in one and kilometres in the other is a common cause.
If the stop itself is in the wrong place, correct `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` for {{stopId}} in `stops.txt`.

stop_without_location.summary: `stop_lat` and/or `stop_lon` is missing for stop with `location_type` equal to`0`, `1`, or `2`
stop_without_location.description: `stop_lat` and/or `stop_lon` are required for locations that are stops (`location_type=0`), stations (`location_type=1`) or entrances/exits (`location_type=2`).

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The faulty record's id.

steps.text: {{stopId}}, line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt`, has no `stop_lat` or `stop_lon`, its latitude and longitude, so it cannot go on a map. Apps need the position to show the stop and plan the walk to it.

fix: Fill in `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` for {{stopId}} in decimal degrees, as a map app gives them (for example 45.5017 and -73.5673).
If {{stopId}} is really a node inside a station or a boarding area, set `location_type` to 3 or 4, which may go without a position.

stop_without_stop_time.summary: A stop in `stops.txt` is not referenced by any `stop_times.stop_id`.
stop_without_stop_time.description: Such stops are not used by any trip and normally do not provide user value. This notice may indicate a typo in `stop_times.txt`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty stop.

stopName.description: The name of the faulty stop.

steps.text: {{stopName}} is in `stops.txt`, the list of stops, but no trip stops there.
Nothing in `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, names {{stopId}}. Apps may still show the stop on their maps, where riders would wait for a vehicle that never comes.

fix: If trips do serve {{stopName}}, add it to their stops in `stop_times.txt`; a mistyped `stop_id` there is a common cause.
If no trip serves it any more, remove {{stopId}} from `stops.txt` (line {{csvRowNumber}}).

stop_without_zone_id.summary: Stop without value for `stops.zone_id` contained in a route with a zone-dependent fare rule.
stop_without_zone_id.description: If `fare_rules.txt` is provided, and `fare_rules.txt` uses at least one column among `origin_id`, `destination_id`, and `contains_id`, then all stops and platforms (location_type = 0) must have `stops.zone_id` assigned if they are defined in a trip defined in a route defined in a fare rule which also defines at least one of `origin_id`, `destination_id`, or `contains_id`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The faulty record's id.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) has no `zone_id`, the fare zone it is in, but a route that stops there has fares that depend on zones.
These are the rules in `fare_rules.txt`; some price a trip by the zones it starts in, ends in or passes through. Without a zone for {{stopName}}, apps cannot work out the fare to or from it.

fix: Set `zone_id` for {{stopId}} in `stops.txt` to the fare zone it is in, one of the zones the fare rules use.

stops_match_shape_out_of_order.summary: Two stop entries are different than their arrival-departure order defined by `shapes.txt`.
stops_match_shape_out_of_order.description: This could indicate a problem with the location of the stops, the path of the shape, or the sequence of the stops for their trip.

match1.description: Latitude and longitude pair of the first matching location.

match2.description: Latitude and longitude pair of the second matching location.

shapeId.description: The id of the shape that is referred to.

stopId1.description: The id of the first stop that is referred to.

stopId2.description: The id of the second stop that is referred to.

stopName1.description: The name of the first stop that is referred to.

stopName2.description: The name of the second stop that is referred to.

stopTimeCsvRowNumber1.description: The row number of the first faulty record from `stop_times.txt`.

stopTimeCsvRowNumber2.description: The row number of the second faulty record from `stop_times.txt`.

tripCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record from `trips.txt`.

tripId.description: The id of the trip that is referred to.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} stops at {{stopName2}} and then at {{stopName1}}, but along its line, shape {{shapeId}}, {{stopName1}} comes first.
Played at its scheduled pace, the vehicle doubles back between {{stopName2}} and {{stopName1}}. Apps that follow it along the line show it jumping backwards.

fix: If the stops are in the wrong order, swap the `stop_sequence` values on lines {{stopTimeCsvRowNumber2}} and {{stopTimeCsvRowNumber1}} of `stop_times.txt`.
If one of the stops is in the wrong place, correct `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` for {{stopId2}} or {{stopId1}} in `stops.txt`.
If the line is wrong, redraw shape {{shapeId}} so it passes the stops in the order the trip serves them.

message.description: The error message that explains the reason for the exception.

steps.text: This is not a problem in the feed's data: the validator failed while running its checks side by side. The rest of the report may be incomplete.

fix: Run the validator again.
If it happens again, report it to the gtfs-validator project on GitHub, with the message above and the error name {{exception}}.

timeframe_only_start_or_end_time_specifi.summary: A row from `timeframes.txt` was found with only one of `start_time` and `end_time` specified.
timeframe_only_start_or_end_time_specifi.description: Either both must be specified or neither must be specified.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number for the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `timeframes.txt`, the times of day a fare applies, has a `start_time` or an `end_time` but not both. Apps cannot tell when the fare starts or stops applying.

fix: Fill in the missing `start_time` or `end_time` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `timeframes.txt`.
If the fare applies all day, empty both `start_time` and `end_time` on line {{csvRowNumber}}.

timeframe_overlap.summary: Two entries in `timeframes.txt` with the same `timeframe_group_id` and `service_id` have overlapping time intervals.
timeframe_overlap.description: Timeframes with the same group and service dates must not overlap in time. Two entries X and Y are considered to directly overlap if X.start_time is less than or equal to Y.start_time and Y.start_time is less than X.end_time.

currCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the second timeframe entry.

currStartTime.description: The start time of the second timeframe entry.

prevCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the first timeframe entry.

serviceId.description: The service id associated with the two entries.

timeframeGroupId.description: The timeframe group id associated with the two entries.

steps.text: Timeframe {{timeframeGroupId}} on service {{serviceId}} has two periods in `timeframes.txt`, the times of day a fare applies. Line {{prevCsvRowNumber}} ends at {{prevEndTime}}, but line {{currCsvRowNumber}} starts at {{currStartTime}}.
From {{currStartTime}} to {{prevEndTime}} the two periods overlap. A timeframe's periods must not overlap, or apps cannot be sure which fare a rider pays.

fix: Set `end_time` on line {{prevCsvRowNumber}} to {{currStartTime}}, or `start_time` on line {{currCsvRowNumber}} to {{prevEndTime}}, so one period ends where the next starts.
If one period was meant to extend the other, merge lines {{prevCsvRowNumber}} and {{currCsvRowNumber}} into one row from the earlier start to the later end.

timeframe_start_or_end_time_greater_than.summary: A time in `timeframes.txt` is greater than `24:00:00`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number for the faulty record.

fieldName.description: The time field name for the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `timeframes.txt`, the times of day a fare applies, has `{{fieldName}}` {{time}}. A timeframe is a time of day, from 00:00:00 to 24:00:00, so unlike a trip's times it cannot run past midnight.

fix: Set `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} to 24:00:00 or earlier.
If the fare applies past midnight, end this row at 24:00:00 and add another row from 00:00:00 for the hours after midnight.

too_many_rows.summary: A CSV file has too many rows.
too_many_rows.description: Feeds with too large files cannot be processed in a reasonable time by GTFS consumers.

filename.description: Name of the CSV file that has too many rows.

rowNumber.description: Number of the row when reading was stopped.

steps.text: `{{filename}}` is too large: the validator stopped reading it at row {{rowNumber}}, so the rest was not checked. Apps cannot load a file this big in a reasonable time.

fix: Make `{{filename}}` smaller by removing rows that are no longer used, such as old trips or services.
If the file is `shapes.txt`, the lines trips are drawn with, simplify the shapes so each has fewer points.

transfer_distance_above_2_km.summary: The transfer distance from stop to stop in `transfers.txt` is larger than 2 km.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `transfers.txt` for the faulty entry.

distanceKm.description: The distance between the two stops in km.

fromStopId.description: The ID of the stop in `from_stop_id`.

toStopId.description: The ID of the stop in `to_stop_id`.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, the changes riders can make between stops, links {{fromStopId}} to {{toStopId}}, {{distanceKm|km}} apart. Few riders walk more than 2 km to change, so it is worth checking.
These are the two stops. If one is in the wrong place, its `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` need correcting; if both are right, the transfer may name the wrong stop.

fix: Check `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` of {{fromStopId}} and {{toStopId}}, since one of them may be in the wrong place.
If the transfer names the wrong stop, correct line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, or delete it if riders do not change there.
If riders really make this {{distanceKm|km}} change, there is nothing to fix.

transfer_distance_too_large.summary: The transfer distance from stop to stop in `transfers.txt` is larger than 10 km.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `transfers.txt` for the faulty entry.

distanceKm.description: The distance between the two stops in km.

fromStopId.description: The ID of the stop in `from_stop_id`.

toStopId.description: The ID of the stop in `to_stop_id`.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, the changes riders can make between stops, links {{fromStopId}} to {{toStopId}}, {{distanceKm|km}} apart. Nobody walks over 10 km to change, so apps would offer a connection riders cannot make.
These are the two stops. If one is in the wrong place, its `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` need correcting; if both are right, the transfer names the wrong stop.

fix: Check `stop_lat` and `stop_lon` of {{fromStopId}} and {{toStopId}}, since one of them may be in the wrong place.
If the transfer names the wrong stop, correct line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, or delete it if riders do not change there.

transfer_with_invalid_stop_location_type.summary: A stop id field from GTFS file `transfers.txt` references a stop that has a `location_type` other than 0 or 1 (aka Stop/Platform or Station).

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `transfers.txt` for the faulty entry.

locationTypeName.description: The name of the invalid location type.

locationTypeValue.description: The numeric value of the invalid location type.

stopId.description: The referenced stop id.

stopIdFieldName.description: The name of the stop id field (e.g. `from_stop_id`) referencing the stop.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, the changes riders can make between stops, has {{stopId}} in `{{stopIdFieldName}}`, and {{stopId}} is an {{locationTypeName|words}}. A change between vehicles has to be at a stop, a platform or a station.

`location_type` is the kind of place: 0 a stop or platform, 1 a station, 2 an entrance, 3 a node inside a station, 4 a boarding area. {{stopId}} is a {{locationTypeValue}}. No vehicle stops at types 2 to 4, so apps cannot offer the change.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, change `{{stopIdFieldName}}` to the stop or station riders change at, usually the `parent_station` of {{stopId}}.

transfer_with_invalid_trip_and_route.summary: A trip id field from GTFS file `transfers.txt` references a route that does not match its `trips.txt` `route_id`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `transfers.txt` for the faulty entry.

routeFieldName.description: The name of the route id field (e.g. `from_route_id`) referencing the route.

tripFieldName.description: The name of the trip id field (e.g. `from_trip_id`) referencing a trip.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, the changes riders can make, names trip {{tripId}} and route {{routeId}}. But trip {{tripId}} runs on route {{expectedRouteId}}, not {{routeId}}.
In `trips.txt`, the list of trips, {{tripId}} belongs to route {{expectedRouteId}}. With two different routes named, apps cannot tell which one the transfer is for.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, set `{{routeFieldName}}` to {{expectedRouteId}}, or empty it, since the trip already says its route.
If the trip is the mistake, change `{{tripFieldName}}` to a trip of route {{routeId}}.

transfer_with_invalid_trip_and_stop.summary: A trip id field from GTFS file `transfers.txt` references a stop that is not included in the referenced trip's stop-times.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `transfers.txt` for the faulty entry.

stopFieldName.description: The name of the stop id field (e.g. `stop_route_id`) referencing the stop.

stopId.description: The referenced stop id.

tripFieldName.description: The name of the trip id field (e.g. `from_trip_id`) referencing a trip.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, the changes riders can make, says riders change at stop {{stopId}} on trip {{tripId}}. But trip {{tripId}} never stops at {{stopId}}.
These are the stops trip {{tripId}} makes, from `stop_times.txt`, the timetable. {{stopId}} is not among them, so apps cannot offer a change there from that trip.

fix: On line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt`, change `{{stopFieldName}}` to a stop trip {{tripId}} really makes.
If the stop is right, change `{{tripFieldName}}` to a trip that stops at {{stopId}}.

transfer_with_suspicious_mid_trip_in_sea.summary: A trip id field from GTFS file `transfers.txt` with an in-seat transfer type references a stop that is not in the expected position in the trip's stop-times.
transfer_with_suspicious_mid_trip_in_sea.description: For in-seat transfers, we expect the stop to be the last stop-time in the trip sequence for `from_stop_id` and the first stop-time for `to_stop_id`. If you are intentionally using this feature to model mid-trip transfers, you can ignore this warning, but be aware that this functionality is still considered to be partially experimental in some interpretations of the spec.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number from `transfers.txt` for the faulty entry.

stopId.description: The referenced stop id.

stopIdFieldName.description: The name of the stop id field (e.g. `from_stop_id`) referencing the stop.

tripIdFieldName.description: The name of the trip id field (e.g. `from_trip_id`) referencing a trip.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `transfers.txt` is an in-seat transfer: riders stay on board while trip {{tripId}} carries on as another trip. But it is set at {{stopId}}, in the middle of trip {{tripId}}.
These are the stops of trip {{tripId}} in order. A vehicle becomes the next trip at the last stop of one and the first stop of the other; set mid-trip, some apps may ignore the transfer.

fix: If the vehicle carries on as the next trip, move the transfer to the last stop of {{tripId}}, or to the first stop of the trip it becomes.
If riders really stay seated mid-trip, for example when a train splits, this can stay as it is.

translation_foreign_key_violation.summary: An entity with the given `record_id` and `record_sub_id` cannot be found in the referenced table.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `translations.txt`, the texts in other languages, translates the row of `{{tableName}}.txt` with id {{recordId}}. No such row exists, so the translation is never used.

fix: Change `record_id` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `translations.txt` to the id of a row that exists in `{{tableName}}.txt`; a typo is the usual cause.
If the row it translated was removed, remove the translation too.

translation_unexpected_value.summary: A field in a translations row has value but must be empty.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

fieldName.description: The name of the field that was expected to be empty.

fieldValue.description: Actual value of the field that was expected to be empty.
