steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `translations.txt`, the texts in other languages, sets `{{fieldName}}` to {{fieldValue}}, but on this row it must be empty.
A translation names the text it replaces either by the row's id, in `record_id`, or by the original text, in `field_value`, never both. With both, apps may ignore the translation.

fix: Empty `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `translations.txt`, and keep the other way of naming the text.

translation_unknown_table_name.summary: A translation references an unknown or missing GTFS table.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `translations.txt`, the texts in other languages, translates a text in a file called {{tableName}}. That is not a file this feed has or one that can be translated, so the translation is never used.

fix: Set `table_name` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `translations.txt` to the file the text is in, without .txt: agency, stops, routes, trips, stop_times, pathways, levels, feed_info or attributions.
If the file it named is not part of the feed, remove the translation.

trip_coverage_not_active_for_next7_days.summary: Trips data should be valid for at least the next seven days.
trip_coverage_not_active_for_next7_days.description: This notice is triggered if the date range where a significant number of trips are running ends in less than 7 days.

serviceWindowEndDate.description: The end date of the majority service window.

serviceWindowStartDate.description: The start date of the majority service window.

steps.text: Most of the feed's trips run from {{serviceWindowStartDate|date}} to {{serviceWindowEndDate|date}}. Checked on {{currentDate|date}}, that does not cover the next seven days, so apps will have few or no trips to show riders.
Service days, opened on {{currentDate|date}}, the day the feed was checked. Look at how many of the days after it have service.

fix: Publish a feed whose services run at least seven days past {{currentDate|date}}, by extending `end_date` in `calendar.txt` or adding the coming days to `calendar_dates.txt`.
If the schedule is about to change, publish the new one now, with the days it starts on.

trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance.summary: The distance between the last shape point and last stop point is greater than or equal to the 11.1m threshold.

geoDistanceToShape.description: The distance in meters between the shape and the stop.

maxShapeDistanceTraveled.description: The faulty record's shape max distance traveled.

maxTripDistanceTraveled.description: The faulty record's trip max distance traveled.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} puts its last stop at distance {{maxTripDistanceTraveled|round}} along its line, but that line, shape {{shapeId}}, ends at {{maxShapeDistanceTraveled|round}}. The last stop is {{geoDistanceToShape|m}} beyond the end.
The points of shape {{shapeId}}, each with its `shape_dist_traveled`: none reaches {{maxTripDistanceTraveled|round}}. Apps cannot draw the end of the trip, and may show it stopping short.

fix: If the line stops short, extend shape {{shapeId}} to the last stop of trip {{tripId}}.
If the distances are wrong, correct `shape_dist_traveled` in `stop_times.txt` so no stop of {{tripId}} is past {{maxShapeDistanceTraveled|round}}.
Check that `stop_times.txt` and `shapes.txt` measure distances in the same unit.

trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance_bel.summary: The distance between the last shape point and last stop point is greater than 0 but less than the 11.1m threshold.

geoDistanceToShape.description: The distance in meters between the shape and the stop.

maxShapeDistanceTraveled.description: The faulty record's shape max distance traveled.

maxTripDistanceTraveled.description: The faulty record's trip max distance traveled.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} puts its last stop at distance {{maxTripDistanceTraveled|round}} along its line, just past the end of shape {{shapeId}} at {{maxShapeDistanceTraveled|round}}. The last stop is {{geoDistanceToShape|m}} beyond the end.
The points of shape {{shapeId}}, each with its `shape_dist_traveled`. The gap is small, often rounding, but apps may draw the trip ending just short of its last stop.

fix: Extend shape {{shapeId}} to the last stop of trip {{tripId}}, or lower that stop's `shape_dist_traveled` in `stop_times.txt` to {{maxShapeDistanceTraveled|round}}.
Check that both files round distances the same way.

trip_headsign_matches_intermediate_stop.summary: Trip headsign matches the name of an intermediate stop, not the last stop.
trip_headsign_matches_intermediate_stop.description: The `trip_headsign` matches the `stop_name` of a stop that is not the last stop of the trip. This may confuse passengers boarding after that stop, since the headsign suggests the vehicle is heading to a stop it has already passed.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record in `trips.txt`.

stopId1.description: The id of the intermediate stop whose name matches the headsign.

stopId2.description: The id of the actual last stop of the trip.

stopSequence.description: The stop_sequence value of the intermediate stop that matches the headsign.

tripHeadsign.description: The headsign value that matches an intermediate stop name.

tripId.description: The id of the trip with the problematic headsign.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} shows "{{tripHeadsign}}" as where it is going, in `trip_headsign`, but {{tripHeadsign}} is only its stop {{stopSequence}}: the trip carries on past it.
The trip in its timetable, with the stops after {{tripHeadsign}}. Riders boarding there would see a sign for a place the vehicle has already passed.

fix: If the trip really ends at {{tripHeadsign}}, remove its stops after stop {{stopSequence}} from `stop_times.txt`.
Otherwise set `trip_headsign` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `trips.txt` to the name of its last stop, {{stopId2}}.
If the sign should change along the way, as on a loop, set `stop_headsign` in `stop_times.txt` for the stops where it differs.

trip_with_shape_dist_traveled_but_no_sha.summary: A trip has shape_dist_traveled values in stop_times.txt but the shape referenced by the trip's shape_id does not have shape_dist_traveled values on all of its points in shapes.txt.
trip_with_shape_dist_traveled_but_no_sha.description:
When stop times define distance values but the shape does not carry matching distances on every point, consumers cannot use those distances to align stops to the shape geometry reliably. This inconsistency may cause incorrect routing or display behaviour.

Note: Only the first stop time carrying a shape_dist_traveled value is referenced in the notice; this is a representative row rather than an exhaustive list.

shapeId.description: The shape_id referenced by the trip.

stopTimeCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the first stop_times.txt record for this trip that contains a shape_dist_traveled value. Provided as a representative location; other stop times for the same trip may also carry distance values.

tripCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record in trips.txt.

tripId.description: The trip_id of the faulty trip.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} gives its stops a distance along its line, in `shape_dist_traveled`, but its line, shape {{shapeId}}, does not give all of its points one.
The points of shape {{shapeId}}: some have no distance. Without distances on both sides, apps cannot use them to line the stops up with the line.

fix: Add `shape_dist_traveled` to every point of shape {{shapeId}} in `shapes.txt`, measured in the same unit as `stop_times.txt`.
If you cannot measure them, remove `shape_dist_traveled` from the stops of trip {{tripId}} in `stop_times.txt`; apps then place the stops by their location.

u_r_i_syntax_error.summary: A string could not be parsed as a URI reference.

message.description: The error message that explains the reason for the exception.

steps.text: This is not a problem in the feed's data: the validator was given a web address it could not read, usually the one the feed was to be downloaded from.

fix: Check the feed's web address, replace spaces and other unusual characters, and run the validator again.
If the address is correct and it happens again, report it to the gtfs-validator project on GitHub, with the message above and the error name {{exception}}.

unexpected_enum_value.summary: An enum has an unexpected value.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

fieldName.description: The name of the field where the error occurred.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

steps.text: Line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` gives `{{fieldName}}` the value {{fieldValue}}, which is not one of the values GTFS allows in this column. Apps may not know what it means, and may skip the row or treat it as something else.
Each value in this column is a code with a fixed meaning. The list below shows the codes GTFS allows and what each one means.

fix: Replace {{fieldValue}} in `{{fieldName}}` on line {{csvRowNumber}} of `{{filename}}` with the allowed code that describes the row, from the list in the card.
If the value comes from an extension of GTFS that some apps understand, check that the apps that matter to your riders read it.

fieldName.description: The name of the unknown column.

filename.description: The name of the faulty file.

index.description: The index of the faulty column.

steps.text: Column {{index}} of `{{filename}}`, `{{fieldName}}`, is not one GTFS defines. Apps ignore it, so what it holds never reaches riders.

fix: If `{{fieldName}}` is a misspelling of a GTFS column, correct the name in the header.
If it is your own extra data, it can stay, because it does no harm.

filename.description: The name of the unknown file.

steps.text: `{{filename}}` is not a file GTFS defines. Apps ignore it, so what it holds never reaches riders.

fix: If `{{filename}}` is a misspelling of a GTFS file name, rename it.
If it is your own extra data, it can stay, because it does no harm.

unsorted_stop_times.summary: Stop times are not sorted by trip_id and stop_sequence.
unsorted_stop_times.description: 'stop_times.txt' entries for a given trip are not sorted by stop_sequence, or are not contiguous in the file.

endCsvRowNumber.description: CSV row number of the last stop_times entry for this trip.

startCsvRowNumber.description: CSV row number of the first stop_times entry for this trip.

steps.text: The stops of trip {{tripId}} run from line {{startCsvRowNumber}} to line {{endCsvRowNumber}} of `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, but not together in stop order: other rows sit between them, or they are shuffled.
The trip itself is fine, and most apps sort the rows. Some tools read the file in order, though, and are slower or misread a trip whose rows are scattered.

fix: Sort `stop_times.txt` by `trip_id`, then `stop_sequence`, so the rows of {{tripId}} sit together in stop order.

unsupported_feature_type.summary: An unsupported feature type is used in the `locations.geojson` file.
unsupported_feature_type.description: Use `Feature` instead to comply with the spec.

featureId.description: The id of the faulty record.

featureIndex.description: The value of the unsupported GeoJSON type.

featureType.description: The feature type of the faulty record.

steps.text: Zone {{featureId}} in `locations.geojson`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, gives its `type` as {{featureType}}. Every zone must say exactly Feature, or apps skip it.

fix: In `locations.geojson`, change the `type` of zone {{featureId}} from {{featureType}} to Feature.

unsupported_geo_json_type.summary: An unsupported GeoJSON type is used in the `locations.geojson` file.
unsupported_geo_json_type.description: Use `FeatureCollection` instead to comply with the spec.

geoJsonType.description: The value of the unsupported GeoJSON type.

message.description: The detailed message describing the error.

steps.text: `locations.geojson`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, says at the top that it is a {{geoJsonType}}. GTFS needs a FeatureCollection, a list of zones, so apps cannot read any zone from it.

fix: Wrap the content of `locations.geojson` in a FeatureCollection, written as { "type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [ ... ] } with each zone inside the brackets.

unsupported_geometry_type.summary: A GeoJSON feature has an unsupported geometry type in `locations.geojson`.
unsupported_geometry_type.description: Each feature must have a geometry type that is supported by the GTFS spec. The supported geometry types `Polygon` and `MultiPolygon`.

featureId.description: The id of the faulty record.

featureIndex.description: The index of the feature in the feature collection.

geometryType.description: The geometry type of the faulty record.

steps.text: Zone {{featureId}} in `locations.geojson`, the file of zones that on-demand trips serve, is drawn as a {{geometryType}}. A zone must be an area, a Polygon or MultiPolygon, or apps cannot tell who is inside it.

fix: Redraw zone {{featureId}} as a Polygon, or a MultiPolygon for several areas, that encloses the area served, and export `locations.geojson` again.

unusable_trip.summary: Trips must have more than one stop to be usable.
unusable_trip.description: A trip must visit more than one stop in stop_times.txt to be usable by passengers for boarding and alighting.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} has fewer than two stops, so no one can ride it from one stop to another. Apps leave it out of journey plans.
Its rows in `stop_times.txt`, the timetable: one row per stop each trip makes. There is one at most.

fix: Add the missing stops of trip {{tripId}} to `stop_times.txt`, so it has at least two.
If the trip no longer runs, remove line {{csvRowNumber}} from `trips.txt`.

unused_parent_station.description: A stop has `location_type` STATION (1) but does not appear in any stop's `parent_station`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty stop.

stopName.description: The name of the faulty stop.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) is a station, the row that groups a station's platforms and entrances in `stops.txt`. But nothing belongs to it, so it groups nothing.
No row of `stops.txt` has {{stopId}} as its `parent_station`. Vehicles stop at platforms, not stations, so riders cannot board at {{stopName}} as it stands.

fix: If riders board at {{stopName}}, set the `parent_station` of its platforms to {{stopId}}.
If vehicles stop right at {{stopName}}, make it a stop by setting its `location_type` to 0.
If {{stopName}} is not used, delete line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt`.

unused_shape.summary: Shape is not used in GTFS file `trips.txt`.
unused_shape.description: All records defined by GTFS `shapes.txt` should be used in `trips.txt`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Shape {{shapeId}} is a line in `shapes.txt`, the file of lines trips are drawn with on a map, but no trip is drawn with it.
No row of `trips.txt`, the list of trips, names {{shapeId}} in its `shape_id` column. Riders never see this line: it may be left over, or meant for a trip that lost it.

fix: If a trip should follow this line, set its `shape_id` to {{shapeId}} in `trips.txt`.
If no trip needs it, remove the rows of shape {{shapeId}} from `shapes.txt`.

unused_station.description: A stop has `location_type` STATION (1) but does not appear in any stop's `parent_station`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty stop.

stopName.description: The name of the faulty stop.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) is a station, the row that groups a station's platforms and entrances in `stops.txt`. But nothing belongs to it, so it groups nothing.
No row of `stops.txt` has {{stopId}} as its `parent_station`. Vehicles stop at platforms, not stations, so riders cannot board at {{stopName}} as it stands.

fix: If riders board at {{stopName}}, set the `parent_station` of its platforms to {{stopId}}.
If vehicles stop right at {{stopName}}, make it a stop by setting its `location_type` to 0.
If {{stopName}} is not used, delete line {{csvRowNumber}} of `stops.txt`.

unused_trip.summary: Trip is not be used in `stop_times.txt`
unused_trip.description: Trips should be referred to at least once in `stop_times.txt`.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

steps.text: Trip {{tripId}} is in `trips.txt`, the list of trips, but it has no stops and no times, so riders never see it.
Nothing in `stop_times.txt`, the timetable, has `trip_id` {{tripId}}. It is often left over from editing, or a sign the trip's times were lost.

fix: If the trip runs, add its stops and times to `stop_times.txt` with `trip_id` {{tripId}}.
If it does not run, remove line {{csvRowNumber}} from `trips.txt`.

wrong_parent_location_type.summary: Incorrect type of the parent location.
wrong_parent_location_type.description:
Value of field `location_type` of parent found in field `parent_station` is invalid.

According to spec

- _Stop/platform_ can only have _Station_ as parent - _Station_ can NOT have a parent - _Entrance/exit_ or _generic node_ can only have _Station_ as parent - _Boarding Area_ can only have _Platform_ as parent

Any other combination raise this error.

csvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record.

expectedLocationType.description: The expected location type of the faulty record.

parentCsvRowNumber.description: The row number of the faulty record's parent.

parentLocationType.description: The location type of the faulty record's parent.

parentStation.description: The id of the faulty record's parent station.

parentStopName.description: The stop name of the faulty record's parent.

stopId.description: The id of the faulty record.

steps.text: {{stopName}} ({{stopId}}) names {{parentStopName}} ({{parentStation}}) as its `parent_station`, but that is the wrong kind of place for it to belong to.

`location_type` is the kind of place: 0 a stop or platform, 1 a station, 2 an entrance, 3 a node inside a station, 4 a boarding area. {{stopId}} is a {{locationType}}, so its parent should be a {{expectedLocationType}}, not a {{parentLocationType}}.

fix: Set `parent_station` of {{stopId}} to a row with `location_type` {{expectedLocationType}}, such as the station it is in.
If {{parentStation}} is the right parent, correct the `location_type` of one of the two rows.
